restaurant.name: Borivali Biryani Centre
restaurant.tagline: Dum biryani, tandoor, handi gravies and Indo-Chinese from Borivali West.

dishes.name: Veg Dum Biryani
dishes.short_description: Classic dum-cooked basmati rice layered with mixed vegetables, gently spiced and fragrant.
dishes.long_description: Veg Dum Biryani is basmati rice and mixed vegetables sealed and slow-cooked on dum, so the steam carries the masala through every grain. It tastes fragrant and mildly spiced, with soft vegetables and fluffy rice. Guests usually eat it with raita or papad. It suits anyone who wants a satisfying vegetarian biryani. It comes in Small, Big and Large: Small is roughly one person, Big is about two, and Large is a party portion.

dishes.name: Paneer Tikka Biryani
dishes.short_description: Biryani layered with smoky tandoori-style paneer tikka cubes and fragrant rice.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Tikka Biryani pairs dum-cooked basmati rice with paneer cubes that are marinated and grilled in the tandoor style first. The paneer stays soft inside with a lightly charred, tangy-spiced edge, and the rice is fragrant and moist. Eat it with boondi or veg raita to cool the masala. A good pick for paneer lovers. It comes in Big, about two people, and Large, a party portion.

dishes.name: Paneer Kalimirch Biryani
dishes.short_description: Paneer biryani with a warm black pepper kick instead of heavy chilli heat.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Kalimirch Biryani layers soft paneer with basmati rice flavoured mainly by freshly crushed black pepper. The heat is a gentle, warming bite rather than a chilli burn, and the paneer stays creamy against the fragrant rice. It goes nicely with a cooling raita or chaas. Choose it if you like peppery flavours and a vegetarian biryani that feels a little different from the usual masala style.

dishes.name: Paneer Biryani
dishes.short_description: Simple, fragrant biryani with soft paneer cubes folded through spiced basmati rice.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Biryani is basmati rice cooked with cubes of paneer, onions and biryani spices. The paneer is soft and mild, the rice fragrant and lightly spiced, so the flavour is comforting rather than fiery. It is usually eaten with raita and papad, and the cool yogurt sits well with it. A good everyday vegetarian biryani for people who like paneer but want a straightforward, balanced taste.

dishes.name: Chote Aloo Mushroom Biryani
dishes.short_description: Biryani with baby potatoes and mushrooms soaking up the masala and rice aroma.
dishes.long_description: Chote Aloo Mushroom Biryani combines small baby potatoes and button mushrooms with fragrant basmati rice and biryani masala. The potatoes turn soft and absorb the spices, while the mushrooms add an earthy, meaty bite. It tastes savoury and gently spiced, and goes well with boondi raita or papad. A good choice for vegetarians who want something hearty without paneer.

dishes.name: Soya Chaap Tikka Biryani
dishes.short_description: Biryani topped with grilled, marinated soya chaap pieces for a chewy, meaty bite.
dishes.long_description: Soya Chaap Tikka Biryani pairs dum-cooked basmati rice with soya chaap pieces that are marinated and grilled tikka style. The chaap is chewy and savoury with a smoky, spiced coating, a bit like a meat texture without any meat. It tastes bold and tangy against the soft rice. Eat it with raita or chaas. Good for vegetarians who enjoy a firmer, hearty bite.

dishes.name: Veg Cheese Tawa Rice
dishes.short_description: Tawa-tossed spiced rice with vegetables and melted cheese, rich and cheesy.
dishes.long_description: Veg Cheese Tawa Rice is rice tossed on a hot tawa with chopped vegetables, a spiced masala and a generous finish of melted cheese. It is soft, spicy and rich, with a street-style taste that is quite different from a dum biryani. It is usually eaten on its own or with raita and a cold drink. A good fit for guests who like cheesy, comforting rice.

dishes.name: Dal Khichdi
dishes.short_description: Soft rice and yellow lentils cooked together, mild, soothing and homely.
dishes.long_description: Dal Khichdi is a simple comfort dish of rice and yellow lentils cooked until soft and porridge-like, lightly seasoned with turmeric and salt. It tastes mild, warm and homely, and is easy on the stomach. Most people eat it with papad, raita or chaas, and a spoon of ghee on top is common. It suits anyone wanting a light, soothing meal, including kids and anyone who dislikes heat.

dishes.name: Dal Khichdi Tadka
dishes.short_description: Rice and lentil khichdi finished with a sizzling garlic and cumin tadka.
dishes.long_description: Dal Khichdi Tadka is the same soft rice and lentil khichdi, topped with a hot tempering of ghee, garlic, cumin and red chilli. The tadka adds a smoky aroma and a gentle kick over the mellow khichdi underneath. Eat it with papad, veg raita or chaas. It suits guests who want comfort food with a little more flavour than the plain khichdi, and it is still easy to eat.

dishes.name: Palak Khichdi
dishes.short_description: Rice and lentil khichdi cooked with spinach, mild, earthy and gently green.
dishes.long_description: Palak Khichdi is the classic rice and lentil comfort dish cooked together with spinach, giving it a green colour and a soft, earthy flavour. It is mild and homely, with a little garlic and cumin in the background. Most guests eat it with papad, raita or chaas. A nice choice for people who want something simple and soothing but with a bit of greens in the bowl.

dishes.name: Steam Rice
dishes.short_description: Plain steamed white rice, soft and fluffy, to eat with gravies.
dishes.long_description: Steam Rice is plain white rice steamed until soft and fluffy, with no spices or tempering. It has a neutral, clean taste and is meant to go alongside curries, dal and gravies, soaking up the sauce. It is a good partner for the Mughlai handi dishes and tawa gravies on the menu, and a safe pick for kids or anyone who wants something very mild.

dishes.name: Jeera Rice
dishes.short_description: Fluffy rice flavoured with toasted cumin seeds, mild and aromatic.
dishes.long_description: Jeera Rice is steamed rice tempered with toasted cumin seeds, which gives it a warm, nutty aroma without adding heat. It is soft, fluffy and lightly savoury. It is usually eaten with dal or a Mughlai gravy, where it soaks up the sauce nicely. A good choice when you want something a little more flavourful than plain steam rice but still gentle on the palate.

dishes.name: Biryani Rice
dishes.short_description: Fragrant biryani-style rice served without the vegetables or meat.
dishes.long_description: Biryani Rice is the spiced, fragrant rice of the biryani served on its own, without the vegetable or meat layers. It is lightly flavoured with whole spices and aromatic, and goes well beside a gravy or raita. Choose it if you want the biryani flavour as a side, or want to pair it with a handi or tawa gravy from the menu.

dishes.name: Veg Pulav
dishes.short_description: Mildly spiced rice cooked with mixed vegetables, lighter and softer than biryani.
dishes.long_description: Veg Pulav is rice cooked with mixed vegetables and mild whole spices in a single pot. It is softer and less spiced than biryani, with a gentle savoury flavour and lightly sweet peas and carrots. It is typically eaten with raita, papad or chaas. A good option for guests who prefer a milder rice meal, including kids and anyone avoiding strong masala.

dishes.name: Paneer Mutter Pulav
dishes.short_description: Mild rice pulav cooked with paneer cubes and green peas.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Mutter Pulav is a mild one-pot rice dish cooked with paneer cubes and green peas, seasoned lightly with cumin and whole spices. The paneer is soft, the peas slightly sweet, and the rice fragrant but not spicy. It is usually eaten with raita, papad or chaas. A comforting choice for vegetarians who want something gentler and simpler than a full dum biryani.

dishes.name: Chicken Dum Biryani
dishes.short_description: Slow-cooked dum biryani with tender marinated chicken and fragrant basmati rice.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Dum Biryani is marinated chicken and basmati rice layered and sealed to cook slowly on dum, so the meat turns tender and the rice soaks up the masala. It is fragrant, savoury and moderately spiced, with fried onions and mint through the layers. Guests usually eat it with raita, salad or chaas. It is the best-known biryani on the menu. It comes in Small, Big and Large: Small is roughly one person, Big is about two, and Large is a party portion.

dishes.name: Chicken Tikka Biryani
dishes.short_description: Biryani layered with smoky grilled chicken tikka pieces and spiced basmati rice.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Tikka Biryani layers dum-cooked basmati rice with chicken tikka pieces that are marinated and grilled in the tandoor first. The chicken has a smoky, slightly charred flavour and stays juicy against the fragrant rice. It tastes tangy and well spiced. Eat it with raita or a squeeze of salad onion. It comes in Small, Big and Large: Small is roughly one person, Big is about two, and Large is a party portion.

dishes.name: Afghani Leg Biryani
dishes.short_description: Biryani served with a chicken leg piece in a creamy, mildly spiced Afghani-style marinade.
dishes.long_description: Afghani Leg Biryani pairs fragrant biryani rice with a chicken leg piece in a creamy, mild Afghani-style marinade. The leg is soft and juicy, with a rich, gently spiced coating rather than a fiery one. The rice is aromatic and moist. Eat it with raita and salad. A good pick for guests who like bone-in chicken and want a milder, creamier flavour.

dishes.name: Chicken Tawa Rice
dishes.short_description: Tawa-tossed spiced rice with chicken pieces, quick, hot and savoury.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Tawa Rice is rice tossed on a hot tawa with chicken pieces, onions and spices until everything is coated in masala. It is spicier and drier than a dum biryani, with a slightly smoky, street-style taste. It is usually eaten on its own with raita, salad or a cold drink. A good choice for guests wanting a filling, flavourful rice dish in a hurry.

dishes.name: Chicken Seekh Kebab Biryani
dishes.short_description: Biryani layered with spiced minced chicken seekh kebabs from the tandoor.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Seekh Kebab Biryani layers dum-cooked rice with seekh kebabs made from spiced minced chicken and cooked in the tandoor. The kebabs are soft, juicy and well seasoned, and they flavour the rice around them. It tastes savoury and moderately spicy. Eat it with raita or salad. A good pick if you like kebabs and biryani together in one dish.

dishes.name: Mutton Dum Biryani
dishes.short_description: Rich dum biryani with slow-cooked mutton pieces and fragrant basmati rice.
dishes.long_description: Mutton Dum Biryani is mutton marinated in yogurt and spices, layered with basmati rice and cooked slowly on dum until the meat is soft and the rice is deeply flavoured. It is richer and more robust than the chicken biryani, with fried onions and whole spices. Eat it with raita or salad. It comes in Small, Big and Large: Small is roughly one person, Big is about two, and Large is a party portion.

dishes.name: Mutton Tawa Rice
dishes.short_description: Tawa-tossed spiced rice with mutton pieces, bold, savoury and robust.
dishes.long_description: Mutton Tawa Rice is rice tossed on a hot tawa with cooked mutton pieces, onions and robust spices. It has a bolder, meatier taste than the chicken version, with a slightly smoky, street-style finish. It is usually eaten on its own with raita, salad or a cold drink. A good choice for mutton lovers who want something quick, hearty and well spiced.

dishes.name: Mutton Seekh Kebab Biryani
dishes.short_description: Biryani layered with juicy minced mutton seekh kebabs from the tandoor.
dishes.long_description: Mutton Seekh Kebab Biryani layers dum-cooked rice with seekh kebabs made from spiced minced mutton and cooked in the tandoor. The kebabs are rich, juicy and strongly flavoured, and the rice around them picks up their taste. It is savoury and moderately spicy. Eat it with raita or salad. A good pick for guests who like robust mutton flavour with their biryani.

dishes.name: Kheema Aloo Biryani
dishes.short_description: Biryani with spiced minced meat and soft potato layered through the rice.
dishes.long_description: Kheema Aloo Biryani layers spiced minced meat and soft potato pieces with fragrant biryani rice. The kheema is savoury and well seasoned, and the potato soaks up the masala, giving a hearty, home-style feel. It is moderately spiced and filling. Eat it with raita or salad. A good choice for guests who enjoy kheema and want it in biryani form.

dishes.name: Prawns Kalimirch Biryani
dishes.short_description: Prawn biryani seasoned with crushed black pepper for a warm, peppery bite.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Kalimirch Biryani layers juicy prawns with biryani rice flavoured mainly by crushed black pepper. The heat is warm and peppery rather than chilli-sharp, and the prawns are tender with a light seafood sweetness. Eat it with raita, salad or chaas. A good choice for seafood lovers who like pepper flavour and want a slightly different prawn biryani.

dishes.name: Prawns Biryani
dishes.short_description: Fragrant biryani with spiced prawns and basmati rice.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Biryani is basmati rice layered with prawns marinated in biryani spices, with onions and mint through the rice. The prawns are tender and lightly sweet, and the masala is savoury and moderately hot. Eat it with raita or salad to balance the spice. A good choice for seafood fans who want the biryani experience with prawns instead of chicken or mutton.

dishes.name: Rawas Biryani
dishes.short_description: Biryani with spiced Indian salmon (rawas) pieces and fragrant rice.
dishes.long_description: Rawas Biryani layers basmati rice with spiced pieces of rawas, also known as Indian salmon. The fish is soft and flaky with a mild flavour, and the masala around it is savoury and moderately spiced. Eat it with raita or salad. A good choice for fish lovers who want a biryani with a lighter, more delicate meat than chicken or mutton.

dishes.name: Prawns Tawa Rice
dishes.short_description: Tawa-tossed spiced rice with prawns, quick, savoury and slightly smoky.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Tawa Rice is rice tossed on a hot tawa with prawns, onions and spices until everything is coated in masala. It is drier and more street-style than a biryani, with tender prawns and a savoury, moderately hot taste. It is usually eaten on its own with raita, salad or a cold drink. A good choice for seafood lovers who want something quick and filling.

dishes.name: Anda Biryani
dishes.short_description: Biryani with boiled eggs coated in masala, layered with spiced rice.
dishes.long_description: Anda Biryani layers dum-cooked basmati rice with boiled eggs that are lightly fried and coated in masala. The eggs are soft and savoury, and the rice around them is fragrant and moderately spiced. It is usually eaten with raita, salad or chaas. A good choice for egg lovers, or guests who want a non-veg biryani without chicken, mutton or seafood.

dishes.name: Anda Tawa Rice
dishes.short_description: Tawa-tossed spiced rice with scrambled egg, quick, savoury and filling.
dishes.long_description: Anda Tawa Rice is rice tossed on a hot tawa with egg, onions and spices until everything is coated and lightly browned. It is soft, savoury and street-style, with the egg broken through the rice. It is usually eaten on its own with raita, salad or a cold drink. A good choice for egg lovers who want a quick, filling rice dish.

dishes.name: Kepsa Rice
dishes.short_description: Large party-size spiced rice dish, meant for sharing among a group.
dishes.long_description: Kepsa Rice is a large, party-size spiced rice dish made to be shared around a table. It is fragrant and savoury, with a rice base cooked in spices and meat. Because it is a big portion, it suits groups, family gatherings or office orders. Eat it with raita, salad and a cold drink. Please check the portion with the staff if you are ordering for fewer people.

dishes.name: Chicken Cutlet
dishes.short_description: Crisp, golden shallow-fried chicken patties, soft and savoury inside.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Cutlet is a patty of seasoned minced chicken coated in a crisp crumb layer and fried until golden. The outside is crunchy and the inside soft, savoury and mildly spiced. It is usually eaten as a starter or snack with salad, onion rings and a cold drink, often with ketchup or green chutney. A good pick for sharing and for guests who like a gentle, familiar fried snack.

dishes.name: Kheema Pav
dishes.short_description: Mumbai-style spiced minced meat served with soft, buttery pav.
dishes.long_description: Kheema Pav is Mumbai-style minced meat cooked down with onions, tomatoes and spices into a thick, savoury masala, served with soft pav. It is rich and well spiced, and you tear the pav and scoop up the kheema. It is a filling snack or light meal, often eaten with a squeeze of lime and a cold drink. You can add cheese or extra butter pav.

dishes.name: Omlette Pav
dishes.short_description: Spiced egg omelette with onion and green chilli, served with buttery pav.
dishes.long_description: Omlette Pav is a fluffy egg omelette cooked with chopped onion, green chilli and coriander, served with soft pav. It is simple, savoury and mildly spicy, and you can fold it into the pav like a sandwich. It makes a quick snack or light meal, and goes well with a cold drink. You can add cheese or extra butter pav.

dishes.name: Burjee Pav
dishes.short_description: Mumbai-style spiced scrambled egg cooked with onion and tomato, served with pav.
dishes.long_description: Burjee Pav is Mumbai-style spiced scrambled egg cooked with onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander, served with soft pav. The egg is soft and loose, savoury and a little spicy, and you scoop it up with the pav. It is a quick, filling snack or breakfast-style meal. You can add cheese or extra butter pav.

dishes.name: Brain Burjee Pav
dishes.short_description: Spiced goat brain scramble with onion and tomato, served with soft pav.
dishes.long_description: Brain Burjee Pav is goat brain cooked soft with onion, tomato, green chilli and spices into a scramble-like masala, served with pav. The texture is very soft and creamy, with a rich, peppery, savoury taste. It is a traditional-style delicacy for guests who enjoy offal. Scoop it up with the pav. You can add cheese or extra butter pav.

dishes.name: Add Cheese
dishes.short_description: Add-on: a layer of melted cheese on any of the pav snacks.
dishes.long_description: Add Cheese is an add-on for the pav snacks such as Kheema Pav, Omlette Pav, Burjee Pav and Brain Burjee Pav. Grated cheese is melted over the dish, making it richer, creamier and slightly salty. It is not a separate dish, so order it only alongside a pav snack. A good option for guests who like their snacks cheesy.

dishes.name: Extra Butter Pav
dishes.short_description: Add-on: two extra buttered pav to go with your pav snack.
dishes.long_description: Extra Butter Pav is an add-on of two additional soft pav, toasted with butter, to go with the pav snacks such as Kheema Pav, Omlette Pav and Burjee Pav. They are warm, buttery and soft, and handy for mopping up the last of the masala. It is not a separate dish, so order it alongside a pav snack if you are hungry.

dishes.name: Tulsi Tomato Soup
dishes.short_description: Smooth tomato soup with a gentle holy basil (tulsi) aroma, warm and mildly tangy.
dishes.long_description: Tulsi Tomato Soup is a smooth, warm tomato soup flavoured with tulsi, or holy basil, which adds a light, herby aroma. It tastes mildly tangy and savoury, with no real heat. It is a comforting starter, eaten hot with a spoon before the main course. A good, gentle choice for kids and anyone who wants a light vegetarian soup.

dishes.name: Paya Soup
dishes.short_description: Rich, spiced trotter soup, slow-cooked until silky and deeply savoury.
dishes.long_description: Paya Soup is a rich soup made by slow-cooking goat trotters with spices until the broth turns silky and slightly sticky. It tastes deeply savoury and peppery, with soft, gelatinous meat on the bones. It is usually eaten hot as a starter or a meal on its own, and you can have it with naan or roti. A good pick on a cold day.

dishes.name: Plain Paya Soup
dishes.short_description: Simple trotter soup with a lighter spicing, warm and savoury.
dishes.long_description: Plain Paya Soup is the simpler version of the trotter soup, with a lighter spicing so the flavour of the slow-cooked trotters comes through. The broth is warm, savoury and gently peppery, with soft, silky meat on the bones. It is usually eaten hot, on its own or with naan or roti. A good choice if you like paya but want less masala.

dishes.name: Veg Pepper Spinach Soup
dishes.short_description: Light vegetable soup with spinach and a clear black pepper warmth.
dishes.long_description: Veg Pepper Spinach Soup is a thin, light soup of spinach and vegetables with crushed black pepper. It is green, fresh and savoury, and the pepper gives a warming bite that fades quickly. It is eaten hot as a starter. A good choice for guests who want a light, simple vegetarian soup that is more peppery than sweet or tangy.

dishes.name: Chicken Pepper Spinach Soup
dishes.short_description: Warm spinach soup with shredded chicken and a peppery bite.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Pepper Spinach Soup is a thin soup of spinach and shredded chicken in a chicken broth, seasoned with crushed black pepper. It is warm, savoury and green, with soft chicken pieces and a gentle peppery heat. It is eaten hot as a starter. A good choice for guests who want a light soup with a bit more protein than the veg version.

dishes.name: Prawns Pepper Spinach Soup
dishes.short_description: Light spinach and pepper soup with tender prawns.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Pepper Spinach Soup is a thin, warm soup of spinach and prawns seasoned with crushed black pepper. The prawns are tender and lightly sweet, and the broth is green, savoury and peppery. It is eaten hot as a starter. A good choice for seafood lovers who want a light, clean-tasting soup rather than a thick or spicy one.

dishes.name: Veg Manchow Soup
dishes.short_description: Thick, dark, spicy Indo-Chinese vegetable soup served with crunchy fried noodles.
dishes.long_description: Veg Manchow Soup is a thick, dark Indo-Chinese soup of finely chopped vegetables, with soy sauce, garlic and chilli. It tastes savoury, a little spicy and peppery, and is usually topped with crisp fried noodles that you add as you eat. It is eaten hot as a starter. A good choice for vegetarians who like a bold, hearty soup.

dishes.name: Chicken Manchow Soup
dishes.short_description: Thick, spicy Indo-Chinese soup with minced chicken and crunchy fried noodles.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Manchow Soup is a thick, dark Indo-Chinese soup made with minced chicken, chopped vegetables, soy sauce, garlic and chilli. It is savoury, peppery and a little spicy, and is usually topped with crisp fried noodles. It is eaten hot as a starter. A good choice for guests who want a hearty, filling soup with a proper kick.

dishes.name: Prawns Manchow Soup
dishes.short_description: Thick, spicy Indo-Chinese soup with prawns and crunchy fried noodles.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Manchow Soup is a thick, dark Indo-Chinese soup made with prawns, chopped vegetables, soy sauce, garlic and chilli. The prawns are tender and sweet against a savoury, peppery, mildly spicy broth, and crisp fried noodles go on top. It is eaten hot as a starter. A good choice for seafood lovers who like bold flavour.

dishes.name: Veg Hot N Sour Soup
dishes.short_description: Spicy and tangy vegetable soup with pepper, vinegar and soy.
dishes.long_description: Veg Hot N Sour Soup is a thickened Indo-Chinese soup of finely cut vegetables, flavoured with black pepper, vinegar and soy sauce. It is sharp, tangy and peppery, with a warming heat that opens up the appetite. It is eaten hot as a starter. A good choice for vegetarians who enjoy sour and spicy flavours.

dishes.name: Chicken Hot N Sour Soup
dishes.short_description: Spicy, tangy soup with shredded chicken, pepper and vinegar.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Hot N Sour Soup is a thickened Indo-Chinese soup with shredded chicken and vegetables, flavoured with black pepper, vinegar and soy sauce. It tastes sharp, tangy and peppery, with soft chicken pieces in a warming broth. It is eaten hot as a starter. A good choice for guests who like a sour, spicy soup with some protein in it.

dishes.name: Prawns Hot N Sour Soup
dishes.short_description: Spicy, tangy soup with prawns, pepper and a vinegar edge.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Hot N Sour Soup is a thickened Indo-Chinese soup with prawns and vegetables, flavoured with black pepper, vinegar and soy sauce. The prawns are tender and lightly sweet against a sharp, peppery, tangy broth. It is eaten hot as a starter. A good choice for seafood lovers who like their soup sour and spicy.

dishes.name: Veg Sweetcorn Soup
dishes.short_description: Mild, lightly thickened sweetcorn soup with finely chopped vegetables, gently sweet and savoury.
dishes.long_description: Veg Sweetcorn Soup is a mild, lightly thickened soup of sweet corn kernels and finely chopped vegetables. It tastes gently sweet and savoury with a touch of pepper and no real heat. It is eaten hot as a starter. A good choice for kids and anyone who wants a soft, comforting vegetarian soup without spice.

dishes.name: Chicken Sweetcorn Soup
dishes.short_description: Mild sweetcorn soup with shredded chicken, soft and comforting.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Sweetcorn Soup is a mild, lightly thickened soup of sweet corn and shredded chicken. It tastes gently sweet and savoury, with soft chicken pieces and a touch of pepper. It is eaten hot as a starter. A good choice for kids and for anyone who wants a comforting soup with a little protein and no heat.

dishes.name: Prawns Sweetcorn Soup
dishes.short_description: Mild, gently sweet sweetcorn soup with tender prawns.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Sweetcorn Soup is a mild, lightly thickened soup of sweet corn and small prawns. The sweetness of the corn goes well with the prawns, and the broth is savoury with a touch of pepper and no real heat. It is eaten hot as a starter. A good choice for seafood lovers who prefer a gentle, comforting soup.

dishes.name: Veg Clear Noodle Soup
dishes.short_description: Light clear broth with vegetables and thin noodles, mild and peppery.
dishes.long_description: Veg Clear Noodle Soup is a thin, clear broth with chopped vegetables and soft noodles, seasoned lightly with soy sauce, garlic and pepper. It is light, savoury and mild, not thick like the Manchow soups. It is eaten hot as a starter. A good choice for guests who want a simple, light vegetarian soup with some noodles to eat.

dishes.name: Chicken Clear Noodle Soup
dishes.short_description: Light clear chicken broth with noodles and vegetables, mild and peppery.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Clear Noodle Soup is a thin, clear chicken broth with shredded chicken, vegetables and soft noodles, lightly seasoned with soy sauce, garlic and pepper. It is light, savoury and mild, and easy to eat. It is served hot as a starter. A good choice for guests who want a lighter soup with chicken and noodles, rather than a thick, spicy one.

dishes.name: Prawns Clear Noodle Soup
dishes.short_description: Light clear broth with prawns, vegetables and noodles, mild and clean-tasting.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Clear Noodle Soup is a thin, clear broth with prawns, chopped vegetables and soft noodles, lightly seasoned with soy sauce, garlic and pepper. The prawns are tender and mildly sweet, and the broth is light and savoury. It is served hot as a starter. A good choice for seafood lovers who want a clean, light soup with noodles.

dishes.name: Roti
dishes.short_description: Soft whole wheat flatbread baked in the tandoor, a simple partner for any gravy.
dishes.long_description: Roti is a thin, soft flatbread made from whole wheat flour and baked in the tandoor, with a light char in spots. It is plain and wholesome in taste, meant to scoop up Mughlai handi and tawa gravies, dal or kebabs. It comes Plain or Butter; Butter has a brushing of butter on top. A good everyday bread for guests who prefer something lighter than naan.

dishes.name: Naan
dishes.short_description: Soft, fluffy tandoor-baked leavened bread, pillowy inside with a light char.
dishes.long_description: Naan is a soft, leavened flatbread made from refined flour and baked in the tandoor until puffed and lightly charred. It is pillowy inside with a mild, slightly tangy taste, and is ideal for tearing and dipping into rich gravies. It comes Plain or Butter; Butter has a brushing of butter on top. It goes well with dal, paneer and chicken gravies and with kebabs.

dishes.name: Lacha Paratha
dishes.short_description: Flaky, layered whole wheat paratha with crisp, buttery layers.
dishes.long_description: Lacha Paratha is a layered paratha made by folding and coiling the dough, then cooking it so the many thin layers turn crisp outside and soft within. It tastes rich and wheaty and is great with dal and thick gravies. It comes Plain or Butter; Butter has a brushing of butter on top. A good choice for guests who want something more substantial and flaky than a plain roti or naan.

dishes.name: Garlic Naan
dishes.short_description: Tandoor-baked naan topped with chopped garlic and coriander.
dishes.long_description: Garlic Naan is a soft tandoor-baked naan topped with chopped garlic and fresh coriander before baking. The garlic gives a savoury aroma and a mild, toasty bite, and the bread stays pillowy inside with a lightly charred edge. It comes Plain or Butter; Butter has a brushing of butter on top. It is excellent with paneer, chicken or mutton gravies and dal. A good choice for garlic lovers.

dishes.name: Kulcha
dishes.short_description: Soft, slightly thick leavened bread, baked until lightly golden.
dishes.long_description: Kulcha is a soft, slightly thick leavened bread made from refined flour and baked in the tandoor. It is a little denser and chewier than naan, with a mild taste and light golden spots. It comes Plain or Butter; Butter has a brushing of butter on top. It is usually eaten with chole, dal or a thick gravy, and is a good choice for guests who like a softer bread that holds up to sauce.

dishes.name: Cheese Naan
dishes.short_description: Tandoor-baked naan filled with melted cheese, soft and rich.
dishes.long_description: Cheese Naan is a soft tandoor-baked naan with melted cheese inside, so it comes out gooey, rich and slightly salty. The bread is pillowy with a lightly charred crust. It comes Plain or Butter; Butter has a brushing of butter on top. It goes well with milder gravies, dal or on its own, and it is popular with kids and anyone who likes cheesy bread.

dishes.name: Cheese Garlic Naan
dishes.short_description: Naan with melted cheese and garlic, gooey inside with a savoury aroma.
dishes.long_description: Cheese Garlic Naan combines melted cheese and chopped garlic on a soft tandoor-baked naan. It is rich and gooey with the savoury aroma of toasted garlic, and the bread stays soft with a lightly charred crust. It comes Plain or Butter; Butter has a brushing of butter on top. It goes well with dal and mild gravies, and suits guests who like both garlic and cheese in their bread.

dishes.name: Stuffed Cheese Garlic Naan
dishes.short_description: Naan stuffed with a cheese and garlic filling, generous, soft and rich.
dishes.long_description: Stuffed Cheese Garlic Naan is a naan with a filling of cheese and garlic sealed inside the dough and baked in the tandoor, so each bite is gooey and aromatic. It is the richest and most filling of the naans, with a soft, lightly charred crust. It comes Plain or Butter; Butter has a brushing of butter on top. It is good for sharing, and goes well with dal or a mild gravy.

dishes.name: Veg Raita
dishes.short_description: Cool, whisked yogurt with chopped cucumber, onion and tomato.
dishes.long_description: Veg Raita is whisked yogurt mixed with finely chopped cucumber, onion and tomato, lightly seasoned with roasted cumin and salt. It is cool, creamy and refreshing, and balances the heat of spicy dishes. It is a classic accompaniment to biryani, pulav and kebabs, and works well with tawa rice. A good choice for anyone who wants something cooling on the side.

dishes.name: Pineapple Raita
dishes.short_description: Sweet and tangy yogurt raita with pineapple pieces and a touch of cumin.
dishes.long_description: Pineapple Raita is whisked yogurt mixed with small pieces of pineapple and seasoned lightly with cumin and salt. It is creamy and cool with a fruity, slightly sweet and tangy taste. It pairs nicely with spicy biryani, where the sweetness offsets the heat. A good choice for guests who like a sweeter raita, and it is popular with kids.

dishes.name: Boondi Raita
dishes.short_description: Creamy yogurt with tiny crisp-soft gram flour pearls and roasted cumin.
dishes.long_description: Boondi Raita is whisked yogurt mixed with boondi, which are tiny fried gram flour pearls that soften in the yogurt but keep a slight bite. It is seasoned with roasted cumin, chilli powder and salt. It is cool, creamy and savoury, and a classic partner to biryani and pulav. A good choice for guests who want a raita with a little more texture.

dishes.name: Masala Papad
dishes.short_description: Crisp papad topped with chopped onion, tomato, coriander and masala.
dishes.long_description: Masala Papad is a crisp papad topped with chopped onion, tomato, green chilli, coriander and a sprinkle of chaat masala and lemon. It is crunchy and tangy with a fresh, mild heat. It is usually eaten as a starter or alongside biryani, and is best eaten quickly while the papad is still crisp. A good light snack to share while you wait for the main dish.

dishes.name: Papad Churi
dishes.short_description: Crushed crisp papad tossed with onion, tomato, coriander and spices.
dishes.long_description: Papad Churi is crushed crisp papad tossed with chopped onion, tomato, coriander and spices. It is crunchy and savoury, with a fresh, tangy bite and a little heat from green chilli. It is usually eaten as a starter or snack, or sprinkled over rice dishes for crunch. A good choice for guests who like a light, crunchy nibble before the meal.

dishes.name: Papad
dishes.short_description: Thin, crisp lentil wafer, either roasted or fried, for crunch on the side.
dishes.long_description: Papad is a thin, crisp wafer made from lentil flour and seasoned with pepper. You can choose it Roasted, which is lighter and drier, or Fried, which is crunchier and a little richer. It is a classic side with biryani, khichdi and pulav, and is eaten between bites for crunch. A simple, light choice for any meal.

dishes.name: Green Salad
dishes.short_description: Fresh sliced cucumber, onion, tomato and carrot with lemon, served raw and crunchy.
dishes.long_description: Green Salad is a plate of raw sliced cucumber, onion, tomato and carrot, served with lemon wedges. It is fresh, crunchy and light, with no cooking or heavy dressing. It is eaten alongside biryani, tawa rice and kebabs, where the crunch and freshness cut through rich, spicy food. A good choice for anyone wanting something fresh and light on the side.

dishes.name: Paneer Tikka Dry
dishes.short_description: Soft paneer cubes marinated in spiced yoghurt and grilled in the tandoor, served dry with a light char.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Tikka Dry is the classic tandoor starter: cubes of paneer marinated in spiced yoghurt, threaded with onion and capsicum and grilled until the edges pick up a smoky char. It is served dry, without gravy. The paneer stays soft and milky inside with a mildly spicy, tangy coating. Guests usually share it as a starter with mint chutney and onion rings, or eat it with roti or naan.

dishes.name: Paneer Tulsi Tikka
dishes.short_description: Paneer cubes in a fragrant basil marinade, grilled in the tandoor with a green, herby taste.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Tulsi Tikka takes the usual paneer tikka and changes the marinade to a green basil one, blended with yoghurt, herbs and mild spices. The paneer cubes are grilled in the tandoor until lightly browned at the edges while staying soft in the middle. The flavour is herby and fresh rather than fiery, which makes it a good pick for guests who like milder starters. Enjoy it with chutney, or roti and naan.

dishes.name: Paneer Zafrani Tikka
dishes.short_description: Creamy paneer cubes marinated with saffron and yoghurt, grilled in the tandoor with a gentle sweetness.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Zafrani Tikka uses a saffron marinade, so the paneer cubes take on a golden colour and a gentle, aromatic flavour. They are coated in thick yoghurt and cream with mild spices, then grilled in the tandoor until just set and lightly browned. The result is rich, soft and mellow with very little heat. It suits guests who prefer creamy starters, and works well with naan or as a shared plate.

dishes.name: Paneer Nizami Tikka
dishes.short_description: Paneer cubes in a rich, mildly spiced Nizami marinade, grilled in the tandoor until lightly charred.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Nizami Tikka is paneer marinated in a Nizami-style mix of thick yoghurt, cream and warm spices, then cooked in the tandoor. The cubes come out soft and rounded in flavour, with a smoky edge and a lingering mild spice. It is richer than a basic tikka but not heavy on chilli. Many guests order it as a starter for the table, with mint chutney, onions and a roti or naan on the side.

dishes.name: Paneer Kathi Roll
dishes.short_description: Grilled paneer tikka filling wrapped in a soft flatbread with onions and chutney, a handy hand-held bite.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Kathi Roll is a grilled filling rolled in a flatbread. Here, tandoor-cooked paneer pieces are tossed with onion, capsicum and a tangy sauce or chutney, then wrapped in a soft paratha-style bread. It is easy to eat with one hand, filling without being heavy, and mildly spiced. Guests who want a quick bite or a lighter meal often pick it, with a cold drink or fresh lime soda.

dishes.name: Mushroom Nizami Tikka
dishes.short_description: Button mushrooms in a creamy Nizami marinade, grilled in the tandoor until juicy and lightly smoky.
dishes.long_description: Mushroom Nizami Tikka features whole mushrooms marinated in a thick, creamy Nizami blend of yoghurt, cream and mild spices, then grilled in the tandoor. The mushrooms keep their juice and a slightly meaty bite, while the coating turns lightly golden and smoky. It is rich and mellow rather than hot. A good choice for mushroom lovers sharing a starter, along with chutney and a piece of roti or naan.

dishes.name: Aloo Nizami Tikka
dishes.short_description: Baby potatoes in a creamy Nizami marinade, roasted in the tandoor until tender inside with a golden crust.
dishes.long_description: Aloo Nizami Tikka is potato prepared tandoor-style: small potatoes are marinated in a creamy Nizami mix of yoghurt, cream and gentle spices, then roasted until soft inside and golden outside. It is comforting and mildly spiced, with a faint smoky flavour from the oven. Because potatoes are familiar and filling, this is an easy starter for children and anyone avoiding strong heat. Eat it with mint chutney or alongside roti.

dishes.name: Tandoori Aloo
dishes.short_description: Tandoor-roasted potatoes in a tangy, spiced yoghurt marinade, crisp outside and soft within.
dishes.long_description: Tandoori Aloo is potato cooked in the tandoor with a tangy, red-spiced yoghurt marinade, the everyday tandoori style rather than a creamy one. The potatoes get a slightly crisp, lightly charred skin and a soft, fluffy centre. It tastes zesty with a medium kick from chilli and chaat masala. It is a simple vegetarian starter that goes well with chutney, onions and lemon, or with roti.

dishes.name: Mushroom Tikka
dishes.short_description: Mushrooms marinated in spiced yoghurt and grilled in the tandoor, juicy with a smoky, tangy finish.
dishes.long_description: Mushroom Tikka is mushrooms marinated in the usual tandoori yoghurt mix with chilli, ginger, garlic and spices, then grilled with onion and capsicum. The mushrooms stay juicy and slightly chewy, and the red marinade gives a tangy, lightly smoky taste with moderate heat. Unlike the Nizami version it is not creamy. Guests share it as a starter, squeezing lemon over it and pairing it with chutney or roti.

dishes.name: Soya Chaap Tikka
dishes.short_description: Chunky soya chaap sticks marinated in tandoori spices and grilled, chewy with a smoky bite.
dishes.long_description: Soya Chaap Tikka uses soya chaap, a firm, chewy vegetarian protein often sold on sticks, marinated in spiced yoghurt and grilled in the tandoor. The texture is dense and slightly fibrous, and it takes on the masala well, finishing tangy and smoky with a medium heat. It appeals to guests who want a hearty vegetarian option with real bite. Serve with mint chutney, sliced onion and roti or naan.

dishes.name: Soya Chaap Afghani Malai Tikka
dishes.short_description: Soya chaap in a creamy white Afghani marinade, grilled in the tandoor, soft and mild.
dishes.long_description: Soya Chaap Afghani Malai Tikka combines soya chaap with a white Afghani marinade made from cream, cheese and yoghurt, flavoured with white pepper and cardamom, then grilled in the tandoor. The chaap is chewy yet tender, with a creamy, mellow flavour and almost no chilli. It is a good choice for guests who find red tandoori marinades too spicy. Pair it with naan, or with chutney as a shared starter.

dishes.name: Tandoori Lollypop
dishes.short_description: Chicken wing drumettes marinated in tandoori spices and roasted in the tandoor, juicy and smoky.
dishes.long_description: Tandoori Lollypop is a chicken wing drumette, trimmed so the meat sits at one end like a lollipop, marinated in spiced yoghurt and cooked in the tandoor. The skin is lightly charred and the meat stays juicy and tender, coming cleanly off the bone. It is tangy and smoky with a medium spice level. It is easy to eat with your hands, so guests often order it to share with chutney and lemon.

dishes.name: Tandoori Chicken
dishes.short_description: Classic chicken marinated in red spiced yoghurt and roasted in the tandoor, smoky, juicy and bone-in.
dishes.long_description: Tandoori Chicken is bone-in chicken marinated in yoghurt, chilli and spices, then roasted in the tandoor until the outside is red, smoky and lightly charred and the inside stays moist. It comes as a Half or Full portion; a Half suits one or two guests, while a Full is better for sharing at the table. The taste is tangy and warmly spiced. Eat it with naan or roti, onions and green chutney.

dishes.name: Chicken Tikka Dry
dishes.short_description: Boneless chicken pieces marinated in spiced yoghurt and grilled in the tandoor, served dry and smoky.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Tikka Dry is boneless chicken marinated in a red, spiced yoghurt mix and grilled in the tandoor until the outside has a light char and the inside is still juicy. It is served dry, with onion and lemon, rather than in gravy. The flavour is tangy, smoky and medium in heat. It is one of the most popular starters, and guests share it with mint chutney, or eat it with naan.

dishes.name: Chicken Seekh Kebab
dishes.short_description: Minced chicken blended with herbs and spices, shaped on skewers and grilled in the tandoor.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Seekh Kebab is minced chicken mixed with onion, green chilli, coriander and spices, shaped around a skewer and cooked in the tandoor. The texture is soft and tender with a lightly crisp outside, and the taste is herby and moderately spicy. It is a lighter-feeling kebab than a bone-in dish and easy to eat. Guests commonly order it with roti or naan, green chutney and sliced onions.

dishes.name: Chicken Kathi Roll
dishes.short_description: Grilled chicken tikka pieces rolled in a soft flatbread with onions and chutney, a hand-held meal.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Kathi Roll is a grilled filling rolled in a flatbread. Tandoor-cooked chicken pieces are tossed with onion, capsicum and a tangy sauce, then wrapped in a soft paratha-style bread. It is filling, easy to hold and carry, and has a medium spice level with a smoky taste. A good option for guests who want a quick, satisfying bite rather than a sit-down plate of kebabs.

dishes.name: Jehangir Kebab
dishes.short_description: Tandoor-grilled chicken kebab in a rich, spiced marinade, tender and smoky.
dishes.long_description: Jehangir Kebab is a Mughlai-style chicken kebab, with tender chicken pieces marinated in a rich blend of yoghurt, cream and warm spices, then grilled in the tandoor. The meat is soft with light charring and a deep, mellow spice rather than sharp heat. It is a good choice if you want something richer than a plain tikka. Guests usually share it with naan or roti and a little green chutney.

dishes.name: Murgh Nizami Tikka
dishes.short_description: Chicken tikka in a creamy Nizami marinade, grilled in the tandoor, tender with gentle spice.
dishes.long_description: Murgh Nizami Tikka is chicken marinated Nizami-style in thick yoghurt, cream and mild spices, then grilled in the tandoor. The pieces are succulent and soft, with a mellow, slightly rich taste and a faint smokiness, rather than strong chilli heat. It suits guests who want a gentler tikka than the red tandoori style. Enjoy it with naan or roti, mint chutney and sliced onion.

dishes.name: Chicken Cheese Banjara Kebab
dishes.short_description: Chicken kebab with a cheesy, herby centre, grilled in the tandoor, soft and mildly spiced.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Cheese Banjara Kebab is a tandoor kebab made with chicken marinated in herbs and spices, with cheese in the mix so each piece is soft and a little gooey. The outside is lightly charred, while the inside is creamy and savoury. It is mild to medium in spice, which tends to please children and cheese lovers. Order it with roti or naan, or as a shared starter with chutney.

dishes.name: Tangri Kebab
dishes.short_description: Bone-in chicken drumsticks marinated in spiced yoghurt and roasted in the tandoor, juicy and smoky.
dishes.long_description: Tangri Kebab is made from chicken drumsticks, marinated in spiced yoghurt with ginger, garlic and chilli, then roasted in the tandoor. The meat stays juicy and tender on the bone, with a deep red, lightly charred coating. The taste is tangy and smoky with a medium kick. Guests who enjoy eating with their hands like it as a hearty starter, with chutney, onion and lemon, or roti.

dishes.name: Noorani Kebab
dishes.short_description: Soft chicken kebab in a creamy white marinade, grilled in the tandoor with a delicate, mellow taste.
dishes.long_description: Noorani Kebab is chicken kebab in a pale, creamy marinade of cream, cheese and yoghurt with pepper and mild spices, grilled in the tandoor until lightly golden. It is very tender and gentle in flavour with only a hint of pepper, so it works for guests who dislike heat. It is a rich, soft kebab rather than a charred, tangy one. Serve with naan and green chutney.

dishes.name: Reshmi Kebab
dishes.short_description: Silky chicken kebab in a cream and cashew marinade, grilled in the tandoor, soft and mild.
dishes.long_description: Reshmi Kebab is boneless chicken marinated in cream, cashew paste and gentle spices, giving a silky, soft texture, then grilled in the tandoor until lightly set. The flavour is mellow and slightly sweet-savoury with a hint of cardamom and little chilli. It is comforting rather than fiery, and a safe pick for family tables. Order it with naan or roti and mint chutney.

dishes.name: Mutton Seekh Kebab
dishes.short_description: Minced mutton with onions, herbs and spices, shaped on skewers and cooked in the tandoor.
dishes.long_description: Mutton Seekh Kebab is minced mutton blended with onion, green chilli, coriander and warm spices, moulded onto a skewer and grilled in the tandoor. It is juicy and deeply savoury, with a firmer, richer taste than chicken kebabs and a lightly charred outside. The spice is medium. It is a good fit for guests who enjoy mutton, usually eaten with roti or naan, sliced onion and green chutney.

dishes.name: Prawns Kalimirch Tikka
dishes.short_description: Prawns marinated with crushed black pepper and yoghurt, grilled in the tandoor, firm and peppery.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Kalimirch Tikka is prawns marinated in yoghurt and a generous amount of black pepper, then grilled in the tandoor. The prawns are firm and juicy with a light char, and the black pepper gives a warming, sharp heat rather than chilli burn. It is a starter for seafood lovers. Guests usually squeeze lemon on it and share it with green chutney, or eat it with naan.

dishes.name: Ravas Tulsi Tikka
dishes.short_description: Rawas (Indian salmon) fish pieces in a basil marinade, grilled in the tandoor, soft and herby.
dishes.long_description: Ravas Tulsi Tikka is rawas, also called Indian salmon, cut into pieces, marinated with basil, yoghurt and mild spices, and grilled in the tandoor. The fish is tender, flaky and moist, with a fresh herby flavour and only light heat. It is a good choice if you want a milder fish starter. Squeeze lemon over it and eat it with chutney, or with roti or naan.

dishes.name: Ravas Tikka
dishes.short_description: Rawas (Indian salmon) pieces marinated in spiced yoghurt and grilled in the tandoor, flaky and tangy.
dishes.long_description: Ravas Tikka is rawas, known as Indian salmon, marinated in the classic red tandoori mix of yoghurt, chilli, ginger and garlic, then grilled in the tandoor. The firm fillets cook through with a lightly charred crust and a moist, flaky inside. It tastes tangy with a medium heat. Fish lovers often order it as a starter to share, with lemon, green chutney and onion rings.

dishes.name: Chicken Malai Kalimirch Tikka
dishes.short_description: Chicken tikka in a cream and black pepper marinade, grilled in the tandoor, tender with a peppery finish.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Malai Kalimirch Tikka is boneless chicken marinated in thick cream, yoghurt and crushed black pepper, then grilled in the tandoor. The pieces stay tender and creamy, finishing with a peppery warmth rather than red chilli heat. It sits between the mild creamy kebabs and the spicier red tikka. Guests share it as a starter, with naan or roti and a little green chutney.

dishes.name: Paneer Butter Pepper Garlic
dishes.short_description: Paneer sautéed in butter with crushed pepper and plenty of garlic, savoury and lightly peppery.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Butter Pepper Garlic is paneer pieces tossed in a wok with butter, chopped garlic and crushed black pepper. It is an Indo-Chinese style, but drier and less saucy than chilli paneer. The paneer is soft and rich, with a strong garlic aroma and a peppery warmth. It is easy to share and goes nicely with veg hakka noodles or fried rice, or on its own as a starter.

dishes.name: Paneer Chilli Dry
dishes.short_description: Crisp-coated paneer tossed with onion, capsicum and a spicy soy-chilli sauce, served dry.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Chilli Dry is a favourite Indo-Chinese starter: paneer cubes are lightly battered and fried, then tossed in a hot wok with onion, capsicum, green chilli and a savoury soy-chilli sauce. It is served dry, with just enough sauce to coat. The paneer is soft inside with a slight crispness outside, and the taste is salty, tangy and spicy. Good with veg fried rice or hakka noodles.

dishes.name: Kung Pao Paneer
dishes.short_description: Paneer in a sweet, tangy and spicy Kung Pao style sauce with capsicum and dried red chillies.
dishes.long_description: Kung Pao Paneer is fried paneer tossed in an Indo-Chinese Kung Pao style sauce, a mix of soy, vinegar, a little sweetness and dried red chilli, with capsicum and spring onion. The paneer stays soft inside and takes up a glossy, balanced sauce that is sweet, sour and spicy at once. It is served as a starter, and goes well with veg hakka noodles or fried rice.

dishes.name: Paneer Plum Chilli
dishes.short_description: Fried paneer tossed in a sweet, sour and spicy plum chilli sauce with garlic.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Plum Chilli is paneer cubes fried and coated in an Indo-Chinese plum chilli sauce, which is fruity-sweet, tangy and warmed with chilli and garlic. The sauce clings to the paneer in a glossy coat, giving a pleasant contrast between the soft cheese and the bold flavour. It is less sharp than a plain chilli dish. Order it as a starter, or with veg fried rice or noodles.

dishes.name: Paneer Dragon Chilli
dishes.short_description: Crisp paneer in a fiery red Dragon sauce with garlic, chilli and a hint of sweetness.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Dragon Chilli is fried paneer tossed in a fiery Indo-Chinese Dragon sauce built on red chilli, garlic and soy with a touch of sweetness. It is bolder and hotter than most paneer starters, with a deep red colour and a punchy, savoury taste. The paneer stays soft inside. It suits guests who like heat, and works with veg hakka noodles or fried rice or a cold drink to cool the palate.

dishes.name: Pepper Paneer
dishes.short_description: Paneer tossed with crushed black pepper, onion and capsicum, savoury with a peppery bite.
dishes.long_description: Pepper Paneer is paneer cubes stir-fried in a wok with crushed black pepper, onion, capsicum and a light soy seasoning. The flavour is warm and peppery instead of chilli-hot, with a savoury edge, and the paneer remains soft. It is served fairly dry, so it works as a starter or a side to rice or noodles. Guests who prefer pepper over chilli heat tend to enjoy this one.

dishes.name: Black Bean Paneer
dishes.short_description: Paneer in a savoury, garlicky black bean sauce with a deep, salty-sweet flavour.
dishes.long_description: Black Bean Paneer is paneer cubes cooked in an Indo-Chinese black bean sauce made from fermented black beans, garlic, soy and a little chilli. The sauce is dark, salty and deeply savoury, with a faint sweetness, and it coats the soft paneer evenly. It has a stronger umami flavour than most paneer starters. Pair it with veg fried rice or hakka noodles for a full meal.

dishes.name: Paneer Soya Basil
dishes.short_description: Paneer in a soy sauce infused with fresh basil, garlicky and aromatic with moderate heat.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Soya Basil is paneer tossed in a soy-based Indo-Chinese sauce flavoured with fresh basil, garlic and green chilli. The basil gives a fragrant, slightly peppery lift to the savoury sauce, and the paneer stays soft and absorbent. It is lighter and more aromatic than the red chilli dishes. Order it as a starter or with veg hakka noodles or fried rice.

dishes.name: Sichuan Paneer
dishes.short_description: Paneer in a bold, spicy Sichuan style sauce with chilli, garlic and a peppery kick.
dishes.long_description: Sichuan Paneer is paneer in an Indo-Chinese Sichuan sauce, a red, garlicky, chilli-forward sauce with soy and a hint of vinegar. The paneer is fried and then coated so it stays soft inside and glossy outside. The taste is spicy and tangy with real heat. It is a good pick for guests who like their starters bold, and goes nicely with veg fried rice or noodles.

dishes.name: Veg Manchurian Dry
dishes.short_description: Crisp vegetable balls tossed in a garlicky, tangy soy-chilli sauce, served dry.
dishes.long_description: Veg Manchurian Dry is made of finely chopped vegetables, usually cabbage, carrot and beans, shaped into small balls, fried until crisp and tossed in a garlicky soy-chilli sauce. It is served dry, with the sauce lightly coating each ball. The taste is savoury, tangy and mildly spicy, and it is a familiar choice for kids and families. Eat it as a starter or alongside veg fried rice or noodles.

dishes.name: Veg Crispy
dishes.short_description: Crisp-fried strips of vegetables tossed in a sweet and spicy sauce, crunchy and tangy.
dishes.long_description: Veg Crispy is thin strips of vegetables, such as carrot, capsicum and cabbage, coated in batter and fried until very crisp, then tossed in a sweet, tangy and mildly spicy sauce. The crunch is the main appeal, and it stays light and snackable. It is a good shared starter, especially for guests who like crunchy textures. Pair it with veg fried rice or hakka noodles.

dishes.name: Mushroom Chilli
dishes.short_description: Mushrooms fried and tossed with onion, capsicum and a spicy soy-chilli sauce.
dishes.long_description: Mushroom Chilli is mushrooms lightly battered and fried, then stir-fried with onion, capsicum, green chilli and a savoury soy-chilli sauce. The mushrooms are juicy and slightly chewy with a thin crisp coating. The taste is salty, tangy and moderately hot. It is the mushroom counterpart to chilli paneer, ordered as a starter or as a side with veg fried rice or hakka noodles.

dishes.name: Stir Fried Exotic Veggies
dishes.short_description: Assorted vegetables stir-fried in a hot wok with garlic and light seasoning, crisp-tender and fresh.
dishes.long_description: Stir Fried Exotic Veggies is a mix of vegetables such as broccoli, baby corn, zucchini and bell peppers, tossed quickly in a very hot wok with garlic and light soy seasoning. They stay crisp-tender and bright, with a clean, savoury taste and mild heat. It is the lightest dish in this section, suited to guests who want vegetables rather than fried food. Pair it with veg fried rice or noodles.

dishes.name: Honey Chilli Potato
dishes.short_description: Crispy fried potato fingers glazed in a sticky honey and chilli sauce with sesame.
dishes.long_description: Honey Chilli Potato is potato fingers fried until crisp and tossed in a sticky sweet-spicy glaze of honey, chilli sauce and garlic, finished with sesame seeds. The first bite is crunchy, then sweet, followed by a gentle chilli heat. It is a well-loved snack among younger guests and a good one to share. Eat it as a starter or with veg noodles or fried rice.

dishes.name: Cigar Rolls
dishes.short_description: Crisp fried vegetable rolls shaped like cigars, with a crunchy wrapper and a savoury, mildly spiced filling.
dishes.long_description: Cigar Rolls are crisp fried vegetable rolls: a savoury filling of chopped vegetables is wrapped in a thin pastry sheet, rolled into a cigar shape and deep fried until golden and crunchy. The inside is soft and mildly seasoned. They are usually served with a dipping sauce, and make an easy, kid-friendly starter. Share them at the start of the meal, with a cold drink.

dishes.name: Potato Veggies
dishes.short_description: Potato and vegetables stir-fried in a spicy, garlicky Indo-Chinese sauce, soft and savoury.
dishes.long_description: Potato Veggies is potato pieces cooked together with mixed vegetables in a garlicky, lightly spiced Indo-Chinese sauce. The potatoes are soft and absorb the soy and chilli seasoning, while the vegetables add some crunch. It is a hearty vegetarian starter with a savoury, medium-spicy taste. It is a good fit for guests who like potato dishes and works well with veg fried rice or hakka noodles.

dishes.name: Water Chestnut Corn Paneer in Sauce
dishes.short_description: Paneer, water chestnut and corn in a sauce of your choice, crunchy and soft in one bowl.
dishes.long_description: Water Chestnut Corn Paneer in Sauce combines soft paneer, crunchy water chestnuts and sweet corn kernels, served in a sauce that the guest chooses. Options include Soy Basil, Kung Pao, Plum Chilli Garlic, Black Bean, Onion Pepper or Sichuan. The mix of textures is the highlight, with the sauce setting the flavour and the heat level. It suits guests who want a saucier dish to eat with veg fried rice.

dishes.name: Broccoli Babycorn Paneer in Sauce
dishes.short_description: Paneer with broccoli and baby corn in a sauce of your choice, fresh, crunchy and savoury.
dishes.long_description: Broccoli Babycorn Paneer in Sauce brings together paneer, broccoli florets and baby corn, cooked in a sauce the guest picks: Soy Basil, Kung Pao, Plum Chilli Garlic, Black Bean, Onion Pepper or Sichuan. The vegetables stay fresh and crunchy, and the paneer is soft. It is a more vegetable-heavy choice than most paneer starters. Order it with veg fried rice or hakka noodles to soak up the sauce.

dishes.name: Java Lotus Stem Corn and Paneer in Sauce
dishes.short_description: Crisp lotus stem, corn and paneer in a sauce you choose, with a pleasing crunch.
dishes.long_description: Java Lotus Stem Corn and Paneer in Sauce is a mix of crunchy lotus stem, sweet corn and soft paneer, tossed in the sauce of your choice: Soy Basil, Kung Pao, Plum Chilli Garlic, Black Bean, Onion Pepper or Sichuan. The lotus stem adds a distinctive crisp bite. The final flavour and heat depend on the sauce picked. It goes well with veg fried rice or noodles.

dishes.name: Pepper Babycorn Mushroom
dishes.short_description: Baby corn and mushrooms stir-fried with crushed black pepper, crisp, juicy and peppery.
dishes.long_description: Pepper Babycorn Mushroom is baby corn and mushrooms stir-fried with crushed black pepper, garlic and a light soy seasoning. The baby corn stays crisp and sweet, while the mushrooms add a juicy, earthy bite. It tastes savoury with a warm pepper heat instead of chilli fire. It is a good vegetarian choice for guests wanting something drier and lighter, served alongside veg fried rice or noodles.

dishes.name: Chicken Lollipop Oil Fried
dishes.short_description: Chicken wing drumettes in a seasoned batter, deep fried until golden and crisp, juicy inside.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Lollipop Oil Fried is chicken wing drumettes, the meat pushed down the bone into a lollipop shape, marinated, battered and deep fried until golden and crisp. The meat is juicy and comes easily off the bone. The seasoning is savoury with a gentle chilli kick, and it is served dry with a dipping sauce. Guests share it as a starter, and it is popular with children.

dishes.name: Chicken Lollipop Sichuan Dry
dishes.short_description: Fried chicken lollipops tossed in a spicy, garlicky Sichuan sauce, served dry.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Lollipop Sichuan Dry is chicken wing drumettes fried and tossed in a dry Sichuan-style sauce of red chilli, garlic and soy. The meat is juicy and tender and the coating is sticky, spicy and savoury. It is hotter and more garlicky than the plain fried lollipops. Order it as a shared starter for guests who like heat, with chicken fried rice or noodles on the side.

dishes.name: Chicken Dragon Chilli
dishes.short_description: Crisp chicken pieces tossed in a fiery red Dragon sauce with garlic and chilli.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Dragon Chilli is boneless chicken fried until crisp and tossed in a fiery red Dragon sauce of chilli, garlic and soy with a touch of sweetness. It is spicy and punchy, with a sticky coating over juicy chicken. It is one of the hotter chicken starters, aimed at guests who like strong heat. Pair it with chicken fried rice or hakka noodles and a cold drink.

dishes.name: Lollipop Plum Chilli
dishes.short_description: Fried chicken lollipops glazed in a sweet, tangy plum chilli sauce.
dishes.long_description: Lollipop Plum Chilli is chicken wing drumettes fried until crisp and coated in a plum chilli sauce, which is fruity, sweet, tangy and gently spicy. The glaze is sticky and glossy, balancing the savoury juicy chicken. It is easy to share and pleases guests who like sweet and sour flavours more than heavy heat. Eat it as a starter, or with chicken fried rice.

dishes.name: Apple Chicken
dishes.short_description: Sweet-and-sour fried chicken in a glossy, tangy sauce with a gentle sweetness.
dishes.long_description: Apple Chicken is sweet-and-sour fried chicken: boneless pieces are battered, fried and tossed in a glossy sauce that is sweet and tangy with a little heat. The chicken is crisp outside and tender inside, and the sauce is gentler than the red chilli dishes. It tends to appeal to children and guests who prefer sweeter flavours. Order it with chicken fried rice or hakka noodles.

dishes.name: Drums of Heaven
dishes.short_description: Chicken wing drumettes in a sticky spicy-sweet glaze, crisp outside and juicy inside.
dishes.long_description: Drums of Heaven is chicken wing drumettes fried and coated in a sticky spicy-sweet glaze with garlic, chilli and soy. The meat is juicy and falls off the bone, and the glaze gives a balance of sweet, hot and savoury flavours. It is finger food by nature. Guests share it as a starter, and it goes nicely with a cold drink or fresh lime soda.

dishes.name: Chicken Chilli
dishes.short_description: Crisp boneless chicken tossed with onion, capsicum and a hot soy-chilli sauce, served dry.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Chilli is one of the most popular Indo-Chinese starters: boneless chicken is battered and fried, then tossed with onion, capsicum, green chilli and a savoury soy-chilli sauce. It is served dry, with the sauce lightly coating the chicken. The taste is salty, tangy and spicy, with a nice contrast of crisp and juicy. Order it with chicken fried rice or hakka noodles.

dishes.name: Kung Pao Chicken
dishes.short_description: Chicken in a sweet, sour and spicy Kung Pao style sauce with capsicum and dried red chillies.
dishes.long_description: Kung Pao Chicken is boneless chicken fried and tossed in an Indo-Chinese Kung Pao style sauce of soy, vinegar, a little sugar and dried red chilli, with capsicum and spring onion. The sauce is glossy and balanced between sweet, sour and hot. The chicken is tender with a light crisp coating. It is served as a starter, and goes well with chicken fried rice or noodles.

dishes.name: Chicken Manchurian Dry
dishes.short_description: Fried chicken pieces tossed in a garlicky, tangy Manchurian sauce, served dry.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Manchurian Dry is chicken pieces coated in batter, fried and tossed in a dry Manchurian sauce of garlic, ginger, soy and green chilli, finished with spring onion. The chicken is juicy under a light crisp coat, and the flavour is savoury, tangy and mildly spicy. It is a familiar crowd-pleaser, easy to share. Order it with chicken fried rice or hakka noodles.

dishes.name: Pepper Chicken
dishes.short_description: Chicken stir-fried with crushed black pepper, onion and capsicum, savoury with a peppery warmth.
dishes.long_description: Pepper Chicken is boneless chicken stir-fried in a hot wok with crushed black pepper, onion, capsicum, garlic and soy. The chicken is tender and juicy with a spicy, peppery warmth that builds rather than burns. It is served fairly dry, so it works as a starter or as a side to rice or noodles. Guests who like pepper over chilli heat often prefer it.

dishes.name: Black Bean Chicken
dishes.short_description: Chicken in a dark, savoury black bean sauce with garlic, soy and a little heat.
dishes.long_description: Black Bean Chicken is chicken pieces cooked in an Indo-Chinese black bean sauce built from fermented black beans, garlic, soy and a little chilli. The sauce is dark, salty and deeply savoury, with the faint sweetness the beans bring, coating tender chicken evenly. It is a good choice for guests who like strong umami flavours. Pair with chicken fried rice or hakka noodles.

dishes.name: Chicken Plum Chilli
dishes.short_description: Fried chicken pieces in a sweet, tangy and mildly spicy plum chilli sauce.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Plum Chilli is boneless chicken fried and tossed in a glossy plum chilli sauce, which is fruity, sweet and tangy with gentle chilli and garlic. The chicken is crisp outside and juicy inside, and the sauce is milder and rounder than a straight chilli dish. It suits guests who want some heat without too much fire. Order it with chicken fried rice or noodles.

dishes.name: Chicken Soy Basil
dishes.short_description: Chicken in a soy sauce scented with fresh basil and garlic, savoury and aromatic.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Soy Basil is chicken pieces tossed in a soy-based Indo-Chinese sauce with fresh basil, garlic and green chilli. The basil gives a fragrant, slightly peppery freshness to the savoury sauce, and the chicken stays tender. It is less fiery than the red chilli dishes and has a more aromatic character. Order it as a starter or with chicken fried rice or hakka noodles.

dishes.name: BBQ Wings
dishes.short_description: Chicken wings coated in a smoky, sweet and tangy barbecue sauce, sticky and juicy.
dishes.long_description: BBQ Wings are chicken wings cooked and coated in a sticky barbecue sauce that is smoky, sweet and tangy. The meat is juicy and the glaze caramelises slightly at the edges. They are eaten with the hands, and make a good shared starter, especially with a cold drink. The spice is mild to medium, so most guests will find them easy to enjoy.

dishes.name: Chicken Crispy
dishes.short_description: Strips of chicken fried until very crisp and tossed in a sweet, tangy and spicy sauce.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Crispy is thin strips of chicken coated in a light batter and fried until very crunchy, then tossed in a sweet, tangy and mildly spicy sauce with a bit of capsicum and spring onion. The crunch lasts through the sauce and the inside stays tender. It is a snackable starter that appeals to most ages. Order it with chicken fried rice or hakka noodles.

dishes.name: Sichuan Chicken
dishes.short_description: Chicken in a bold red Sichuan sauce of chilli, garlic and soy with a spicy, tangy kick.
dishes.long_description: Sichuan Chicken is boneless chicken fried and coated in an Indo-Chinese Sichuan sauce, a red, garlicky, chilli-forward mix with soy and a touch of vinegar. The chicken stays juicy inside and takes on a bold, tangy and fairly hot flavour. It is made for guests who like their starters spicy. Order it with chicken fried rice or noodles to balance the heat.

dishes.name: Fish Chilli
dishes.short_description: Crisp fried fish pieces tossed with onion, capsicum and a spicy soy-chilli sauce.
dishes.long_description: Fish Chilli is boneless fish pieces coated in batter, fried until crisp and tossed with onion, capsicum, green chilli and a savoury soy-chilli sauce. The fish stays soft and flaky under the crisp coating. The taste is salty, tangy and spicy. It is the fish version of the chilli dishes, served dry as a starter, and goes with veg or chicken hakka noodles or fried rice.

dishes.name: Prawns Chilli
dishes.short_description: Fried prawns tossed with onion, capsicum and a spicy soy-chilli sauce, firm and juicy.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Chilli is prawns coated in a thin batter, fried and tossed with onion, capsicum, green chilli and a savoury soy-chilli sauce. The prawns stay firm and juicy with a light crisp coat, and the sauce is salty, tangy and quite spicy. It is a prawn lover's starter, usually eaten with chicken fried rice or hakka noodles, or on its own with a cold drink.

dishes.name: Kung Pao Fish
dishes.short_description: Fish pieces in a sweet, sour and spicy Kung Pao style sauce with capsicum and dried chillies.
dishes.long_description: Kung Pao Fish is boneless fish fried and tossed in an Indo-Chinese Kung Pao style sauce of soy, vinegar, a little sugar and dried red chilli, with capsicum and spring onion. The fish is soft and flaky inside and the sauce is glossy, balanced between sweet, sour and hot. It is a good pick for guests who like fish without too much fire. Pair it with fried rice.

dishes.name: Kung Pao Prawns
dishes.short_description: Prawns in a sweet, sour and spicy Kung Pao style sauce, glossy and juicy.
dishes.long_description: Kung Pao Prawns is prawns fried and tossed in an Indo-Chinese Kung Pao style sauce made from soy, vinegar, a little sugar and dried red chilli, with capsicum and spring onion. The prawns are firm and sweet, and the sauce is sticky and balanced between sour, sweet and spicy. It is a rounded starter for seafood lovers, served with chicken fried rice or noodles.

dishes.name: Fish Plum Chilli
dishes.short_description: Crisp fish pieces glazed in a sweet, tangy plum chilli sauce.
dishes.long_description: Fish Plum Chilli is boneless fish fried and tossed in a plum chilli sauce that is fruity, sweet, tangy and gently spicy. The fish stays tender and flaky under the crisp coating, and the glossy sauce is rounder and milder than a straight chilli sauce. It is a good seafood starter for guests who like sweet-and-sour notes. Serve with fried rice or hakka noodles.

dishes.name: Prawns Plum Chilli
dishes.short_description: Fried prawns in a sweet, tangy and mildly spicy plum chilli glaze.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Plum Chilli is prawns lightly battered, fried and coated in a plum chilli sauce that is fruity, sweet and tangy with some garlic and chilli. The prawns are firm and juicy, and the sauce is glossy and not too hot. It suits guests who want seafood with a sweet and sour flavour. Eat it as a starter, or with chicken fried rice or noodles.

dishes.name: Sichuan Fish
dishes.short_description: Fish pieces in a bold red Sichuan sauce with chilli, garlic and soy, spicy and tangy.
dishes.long_description: Sichuan Fish is boneless fish fried and tossed in a red Sichuan-style sauce of chilli, garlic, soy and a splash of vinegar. The fish stays soft and flaky under a light crisp coating, and the sauce is bold, tangy and fairly hot. It is for guests who like spicy seafood. Pair it with chicken fried rice or hakka noodles to temper the heat.

dishes.name: Sichuan Prawns
dishes.short_description: Prawns in a bold red Sichuan sauce with chilli, garlic and soy, firm, spicy and tangy.
dishes.long_description: Sichuan Prawns is prawns fried and tossed in a red Sichuan-style sauce with chilli, garlic and soy, brightened with a bit of vinegar. The prawns are firm and juicy and the sauce is strong, tangy and hot. It is a punchy seafood starter for spice lovers. Order it with chicken fried rice or noodles, and a cold drink on the side.

dishes.name: Prawns Dragon Chilli
dishes.short_description: Crisp prawns tossed in a fiery red Dragon sauce with garlic and chilli.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Dragon Chilli is prawns fried until crisp and tossed in a fiery Indo-Chinese Dragon sauce of chilli, garlic and soy with a hint of sweetness. The prawns stay juicy and the sauce is sticky, bold and hot. It is one of the spicier seafood starters on the menu. Guests who enjoy heat can pair it with chicken fried rice or hakka noodles.

dishes.name: Prawns Soy Basil
dishes.short_description: Prawns in a soy sauce scented with fresh basil and garlic, savoury and aromatic.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Soy Basil is prawns cooked in a soy-based Indo-Chinese sauce with fresh basil, garlic and green chilli. The basil adds a fragrant, slightly peppery freshness to the savoury sauce, and the prawns stay firm and sweet. It is lighter in heat and more aromatic than the red chilli dishes. Order it as a starter or with chicken fried rice or noodles.

dishes.name: Fish Soy Basil
dishes.short_description: Fish pieces in a soy sauce scented with fresh basil and garlic, savoury and aromatic.
dishes.long_description: Fish Soy Basil is boneless fish tossed in a soy-based Indo-Chinese sauce with fresh basil, garlic and green chilli. The fish stays soft and flaky, and the basil lends a fresh, fragrant lift to the savoury sauce. It is gentler on heat than the red chilli versions, which suits guests who prefer aromatic dishes. Serve it as a starter or with fried rice.

dishes.name: Black Bean Fish
dishes.short_description: Fish pieces in a dark, savoury black bean sauce with garlic and a little heat.
dishes.long_description: Black Bean Fish is boneless fish cooked in an Indo-Chinese black bean sauce made from fermented black beans, garlic, soy and a little chilli. The sauce is dark, salty and deeply savoury, and the fish stays soft and flaky inside. It is a good pick for guests who enjoy strong umami flavours. Eat it as a starter, or with chicken fried rice or hakka noodles.

dishes.name: Pataya Fish
dishes.short_description: Fish pieces in a Thai-style Pataya sauce, tangy, sweet and spicy with garlic and chilli.
dishes.long_description: Pataya Fish is boneless fish in a Thai-style Pataya sauce, a tangy, sweet and spicy mix with chilli and garlic. The fish stays soft and flaky under a light coating and the sauce gives a bright, lively flavour with moderate heat. It differs from the usual soy-led Indo-Chinese dishes. Order it as a starter, or with chicken fried rice or noodles.

dishes.name: Prawns Butter Pepper Garlic
dishes.short_description: Prawns sautéed in butter with crushed pepper and plenty of garlic, rich and aromatic.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Butter Pepper Garlic is prawns sautéed in a hot wok with butter, chopped garlic and crushed black pepper. The prawns are firm and sweet, with a rich buttery coat, a strong garlic aroma and a peppery warmth. It is drier and less saucy than the chilli dishes. A good starter for seafood lovers, eaten on its own or with chicken fried rice.

dishes.name: Brain Butter Pepper Garlic
dishes.short_description: Goat brain sautéed in butter with crushed pepper and garlic, very soft, rich and peppery.
dishes.long_description: Brain Butter Pepper Garlic is goat brain sautéed in butter with chopped garlic and crushed black pepper. The texture is very soft and creamy, and the taste is rich and mild, lifted by garlic and pepper. It is an offal dish, best suited to guests who already enjoy it and know the texture. It is eaten as a starter, often with a squeeze of lemon, or alongside rice or noodles.

dishes.name: Egg Chilli
dishes.short_description: Boiled eggs fried and tossed with onion, capsicum and a spicy soy-chilli sauce.
dishes.long_description: Egg Chilli is eggs, cooked and cut, coated in a light batter, fried and tossed with onion, capsicum, green chilli and a savoury soy-chilli sauce. The egg is soft inside with a thin crisp coating, and the sauce is salty, tangy and spicy. It suits guests who want a non-vegetarian dish without meat or fish. Pair it with veg fried rice or noodles.

dishes.name: Prawns Koliwada
dishes.short_description: Prawns coated in a spiced batter and deep fried, a Mumbai Koli-style crisp and tangy starter.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Koliwada is Koli-style, spiced and batter-fried prawns, a seafood favourite of Mumbai. The prawns are coated in a chilli, ginger, garlic and gram flour batter and fried until crisp outside and juicy inside. The taste is tangy and spicy with a hint of lemon. Guests usually share it as a starter with onion rings and green chutney, alongside a fresh lime soda.

dishes.name: Chicken Koliwada
dishes.short_description: Chicken pieces in a spiced Koli-style batter, deep fried until crisp, tangy and spicy.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Koliwada is boneless chicken coated in a Koli-style spiced batter of gram flour, chilli, ginger, garlic and carom seeds, then deep fried until crisp.
