The chicken stays juicy inside with a spicy, tangy crust. It is a Mumbai street-style snack, usually shared as a starter with lemon and onion rings, or with a cold drink.

dishes.name: Rawas Koliwada
dishes.short_description: Rawas (Indian salmon) in a spiced Koli-style batter, fried crisp with soft, flaky fish inside.
dishes.long_description: Rawas Koliwada is rawas, also called Indian salmon, coated in a Koli-style spiced batter of gram flour, chilli, ginger and garlic, then deep fried. The crust is crisp and tangy, and the fish inside is moist, flaky and mild. It is a popular Mumbai seafood starter for fish lovers. Squeeze lemon over it and enjoy with green chutney and onion rings.

dishes.name: Paneer Koliwada
dishes.short_description: Paneer cubes in a spiced Koli-style batter, fried until crisp outside and soft inside.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Koliwada is the vegetarian take on the Koli-style batter-fried starter: paneer cubes coated in a spiced gram flour batter with chilli, ginger, garlic and carom seeds, then fried until crisp. The inside stays soft and milky and the outside is tangy and spicy. Guests share it as a starter with lemon, onion rings and green chutney, or a cold drink.

dishes.name: Paneer Angara
dishes.short_description: Paneer cubes in a smoky, fiery red gravy with a strong chilli kick.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Angara is soft paneer cooked in a smoky, fiery red gravy that gets its name from glowing coals. The masala is thick, deep red and clearly spicy, with a charred, roasted note running through it. Tear a piece of naan, roti or lacha paratha and scoop it up, then cool your mouth with a glass of chaas or lassi, or a side of raita. It suits guests who like their vegetarian dishes bold and hot.

dishes.name: Paneer Do Pyaza
dishes.short_description: Paneer in a thick onion masala, with onions added twice for sweetness and bite.
dishes.long_description: Do Pyaza means onions added twice, and that is the idea here. Paneer cubes sit in a thick masala built on cooked-down onion, with more onion pieces added later so you get both a sweet, mellow gravy and some crunch. It is medium in spice and homely in flavour. Eat it with roti, lacha paratha or naan, and a bowl of raita on the side. A good pick for onion lovers and everyday vegetarian meals.

dishes.name: Paneer Kolhapuri
dishes.short_description: Paneer in a hot, spicy Maharashtrian-style red chilli and coconut gravy.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Kolhapuri brings the heat of Kolhapur-style cooking: a hot, spicy gravy made with red chilli and coconut, with paneer cubes soaked in it. The sauce is thin-to-medium, deep red and punchy, with a warm, nutty background from the coconut. Roti, lacha paratha or naan are the usual partners, and chaas or lassi helps if the spice builds. Choose it if you enjoy proper heat and want a vegetarian dish with some fire.

dishes.name: Butter Paneer
dishes.short_description: Soft paneer in a creamy tomato-butter gravy, mild, rich and gently sweet.
dishes.long_description: Butter Paneer is one of the most ordered vegetarian dishes. Soft paneer cubes come in a smooth makhani-style gravy of tomato, butter and cream, mild in spice and slightly sweet. The sauce is silky and coats a piece of naan or garlic naan perfectly; roti and jeera rice work well too. Add raita, chaas or lassi alongside. It is an easy choice for first-timers, families and anyone who prefers gentle flavours over heat.

dishes.name: Paneer Tikka Masala
dishes.short_description: Tandoor-grilled paneer tikka in a spiced, creamy tomato-onion masala.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Tikka Masala starts with paneer marinated and grilled in the tandoor, then simmered in a thick onion-tomato masala finished with a little cream. You get a light smoky char on the paneer against a rounded, medium-spiced gravy. It is thicker and more savoury than butter paneer. Pair it with naan, garlic naan, roti or jeera rice, and raita or lassi to balance it. A good choice for guests who want something flavourful without it being too hot.

dishes.name: Palak Paneer
dishes.short_description: Paneer cubes in a smooth, mildly spiced spinach gravy.
dishes.long_description: Palak Paneer is paneer cooked in a smooth puree of spinach, with garlic, onion and gentle spices. The gravy is green, creamy and mild with a fresh, earthy taste. It goes well with roti, naan or garlic naan, and jeera rice also works nicely. Raita, chaas or lassi on the side round it off. It suits guests who like greens in their meal and prefer a calm, mild curry over a spicy one.

dishes.name: Paneer Karhai
dishes.short_description: Paneer with chunky capsicum in a wok-style tomato and black pepper masala.
dishes.long_description: Karhai means wok-style cooking, and this version cooks paneer quickly in a tomato-pepper masala with big pieces of capsicum and onion. The gravy is thick, tangy and peppery, with a fresh bite from the vegetables rather than a smooth, creamy finish. It is medium-hot. Roti, lacha paratha or naan are the natural partners, with raita or chaas alongside. Suited to guests who like a robust, slightly tangy paneer dish.

dishes.name: Paneer Makhani
dishes.short_description: Paneer in a velvety makhani gravy of tomato, butter and cream.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Makhani is paneer served in the classic makhani style: tomatoes cooked down with butter and cream into a velvety, orange-red gravy. It is mild, rich and a little sweet, with a buttery finish. Mop it up with naan, garlic naan or roti, or spoon it over jeera rice. Raita, chaas or lassi make a nice side. A comforting, low-heat choice for kids, families and anyone who wants a creamy vegetarian curry.

dishes.name: Paneer Tawa Khurchan
dishes.short_description: Scraped paneer and capsicum tossed on the tawa in a thick, spiced masala.
dishes.long_description: Tawa Khurchan means scraped or crumbled, tawa-fried food. Here paneer is cut and scraped into strips and tossed on a hot tawa with onion, capsicum and a thick masala, so the result is drier and more textured than a regular gravy. The flavour is savoury and medium-spiced with a toasty edge. It is best with roti, lacha paratha or naan, and some raita. Choose it if you prefer a thick, almost semi-dry paneer dish.

dishes.name: Paneer Motiwala
dishes.short_description: Paneer in a rich, creamy gravy, smooth and mildly spiced.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Motiwala is a rich and creamy paneer dish with a smooth, mild gravy that feels special without being heavy on spice. The sauce is silky and coats the paneer evenly, with a gentle sweetness from cream and cashew. It goes best with naan, garlic naan or roti, and jeera rice is a good match too. Raita, chaas or lassi complete the meal. A fine choice for guests who like creamy, mellow flavours.

dishes.name: Paneer Pasanda
dishes.short_description: Paneer in a mild, creamy gravy made with nuts and cream.
dishes.long_description: Pasanda is a mild, creamy gravy thickened with ground nuts and cream, and here it is paired with soft paneer. The taste is delicate, lightly sweet and gentle on the palate, with very little heat. The texture is smooth and rich. Eat it with naan, garlic naan or roti, or alongside jeera rice, with raita or lassi on the side. It suits children, older guests and anyone who prefers a mild, rich curry.

dishes.name: Paneer Mutter
dishes.short_description: Paneer and green peas in a home-style onion-tomato gravy.
dishes.long_description: Paneer Mutter pairs paneer cubes with green peas in a simple onion-tomato gravy. The taste is familiar and homely, medium in spice with a slightly sweet tomato base, and the peas add a soft bite. The gravy is moderately thick, so it works well with roti, naan or garlic naan, or spooned over jeera rice. Add raita, chaas or lassi. A dependable choice for an everyday vegetarian meal.

dishes.name: Aloo Mutter
dishes.short_description: Potatoes and green peas in a simple, homely tomato-onion gravy.
dishes.long_description: Aloo Mutter is a plain, comforting dish of potato pieces and green peas cooked in a tomato-onion gravy with everyday spices. It is medium in spice, a little tangy and not at all heavy. The potatoes soak up the masala and the peas add small pops of sweetness. Eat it with roti, lacha paratha or naan, with raita or chaas alongside. A good budget-friendly pick for anyone who likes simple, home-style vegetarian food.

dishes.name: Aloo Gobi
dishes.short_description: Potato and cauliflower cooked dry-style with onion, tomato and spices.
dishes.long_description: Aloo Gobi cooks potato and cauliflower florets together with turmeric, cumin and a light onion-tomato masala until the vegetables are tender and coated rather than swimming in gravy. The flavour is earthy and mildly spiced with a hint of tang. It is meant to be eaten with roti, lacha paratha or naan, and raita or chaas makes a cooling side. A simple, familiar choice for guests who enjoy dry-style home cooking.

dishes.name: Aloo Methi
dishes.short_description: Potatoes cooked with fresh fenugreek leaves, slightly bitter and well spiced.
dishes.long_description: Aloo Methi cooks potato pieces with fresh fenugreek leaves, garlic and spices into a dry-style, lightly coated dish. Methi brings a pleasant, slightly bitter, aromatic edge that balances the soft, mild potatoes. The spice level is mild to medium. It is best scooped up with roti, lacha paratha or naan, with raita or chaas on the side. A good pick for guests who like leafy, earthy flavours and want something simple.

dishes.name: Veg Karhai
dishes.short_description: Mixed vegetables in a wok-style tomato-pepper masala with chunky capsicum.
dishes.long_description: Veg Karhai is a mix of vegetables cooked wok-style in a thick tomato-pepper masala, with chunky capsicum and onion left with some bite. The gravy is tangy, peppery and medium-spicy, with a fresh, lively feel rather than a creamy one. It goes well with roti, lacha paratha or naan, and raita or chaas helps balance the pepper. A good choice for vegetable lovers who want something robust.

dishes.name: Veg Makhani
dishes.short_description: Mixed vegetables in a creamy tomato-butter makhani gravy, mild and rich.
dishes.long_description: Veg Makhani brings mixed vegetables into the familiar makhani gravy: tomato, butter and cream cooked into a smooth, mild and slightly sweet sauce. The vegetables stay soft and take on the buttery flavour. It pairs well with naan, garlic naan or roti, or with jeera rice, and raita, chaas or lassi alongside. A gentle, comforting choice for vegetarians, children and guests who avoid strong heat.

dishes.name: Veg Tawa Masala
dishes.short_description: Vegetables tossed on a hot tawa in a thick, medium-spiced masala.
dishes.long_description: Veg Tawa Masala is a vegetable dish finished on a hot flat tawa, so the masala turns thick and clings to the pieces instead of forming a loose gravy. You taste onion, tomato and capsicum with a roasted, savoury edge and medium heat. It is best with roti, lacha paratha or naan, plus a bowl of raita. Choose it for a hearty vegetable dish with a bit of punch and a drier finish.

dishes.name: Veg Kolhapuri
dishes.short_description: Mixed vegetables in a hot, spicy red chilli and coconut Kolhapuri gravy.
dishes.long_description: Veg Kolhapuri is a hot, spicy Maharashtrian-style dish of mixed vegetables in a red gravy made with red chilli and coconut. The heat comes up fast and is balanced by a nutty warmth from the coconut. The gravy is moderately thick and deep red. Eat it with roti, lacha paratha or naan, and keep chaas or lassi nearby. It is for guests who enjoy a proper spicy vegetable curry.

dishes.name: Veg Lahori
dishes.short_description: Mixed vegetables in a robust, ghee-rich, well-spiced Lahori-style masala.
dishes.long_description: Veg Lahori is a robust vegetable dish in the Lahori style: a spiced, ghee-rich masala with ginger, green chilli and tomato that tastes bold and full-bodied. The vegetables are cooked until soft and coated in a thick, glossy gravy. It is medium to hot in spice. Scoop it up with roti, lacha paratha or naan, and add raita or chaas to cool things down. A fitting pick for guests who like their vegetable curry hearty.

dishes.name: Sabji Kheema Masala
dishes.short_description: Finely minced vegetables cooked in a thick, spiced kheema-style masala.
dishes.long_description: Sabji Kheema Masala takes vegetables, chopped or minced fine, and cooks them the way mutton or chicken kheema is made, in a thick, dry-ish masala with onion, tomato and plenty of spice. The texture is coarse and hearty, and the taste is savoury and medium-hot. It is a natural fit for roti, lacha paratha or naan, and it also goes well in pav-style meals. Raita or chaas on the side works well. Suits vegetarians who want something hearty.

dishes.name: Diwani Handi
dishes.short_description: Mixed vegetables slow-cooked in a heavy pot in a rich, creamy masala.
dishes.long_description: Diwani Handi is a mixed vegetable handi, meaning the vegetables are cooked in a heavy pot so the flavours come together slowly. The gravy is rich, creamy and medium in spice, with a good variety of vegetable pieces and a mellow tomato-onion base. Serve with naan, garlic naan or roti, or spoon over jeera rice. Raita, chaas or lassi make fine company. A good dish to share at a table where people want one hearty vegetarian curry.

dishes.name: Malai Kofta
dishes.short_description: Soft vegetable and paneer dumplings in a creamy, mildly sweet gravy.
dishes.long_description: Malai Kofta features soft, fried dumplings of paneer and vegetables served in a smooth, creamy gravy that is mild and gently sweet. The koftas are tender inside and soak up the sauce as you eat. The cream and nut-based gravy keeps the spice low. It goes very well with naan, garlic naan or roti, or with jeera rice, and raita or lassi alongside. A good celebratory dish for families and guests who like rich, mild vegetarian curries.

dishes.name: Methi Mutter Malai
dishes.short_description: Green peas and fenugreek leaves in a creamy, lightly sweet malai gravy.
dishes.long_description: Methi Mutter Malai combines green peas and fresh fenugreek leaves in a white, cream-based gravy. The sweetness of cream and peas meets the slight bitterness of methi, giving a mellow dish that is not spicy. The gravy is smooth and moderately thick. Roti, lacha paratha or naan are the usual choices, with raita or chaas on the side. It suits guests who enjoy the taste of methi and like creamy, mild food.

dishes.name: Paneer Bhurjee
dishes.short_description: Scrambled paneer cooked dry with onion, tomato and spices.
dishes.long_description: Bhurjee means scrambled, and Paneer Bhurjee is crumbled paneer cooked with onion, tomato, green chilli and spices until soft and loosely clumped. It has no real gravy: the masala clings to the paneer, giving a savoury, medium-spiced, slightly tangy taste. It is eaten with roti, lacha paratha or naan, and some raita on the side. Well suited to guests who want a quick-eating, dry-style paneer dish with a homely feel.

dishes.name: Spicy Malai Kofta
dishes.short_description: Paneer and vegetable dumplings in a creamy gravy with an extra chilli kick.
dishes.long_description: Spicy Malai Kofta serves the same soft dumplings of paneer and vegetables, but in a creamy gravy pushed up with extra chilli and masala. You still get the smooth, rich texture of cream and cashew, now with noticeable heat running through it. It pairs well with naan, garlic naan or roti, or with jeera rice, with raita, chaas or lassi to cool it. Pick it if you like malai kofta but want more warmth.

dishes.name: Babycorn Mushroom Tawa Masala
dishes.short_description: Baby corn and mushrooms tossed on a tawa in a thick, spiced masala.
dishes.long_description: This dish tosses baby corn and mushrooms on a hot tawa with onion, capsicum and a thick tomato masala. The result is a drier, clingy gravy with a roasted, savoury taste and medium spice. The baby corn stays a little crunchy while the mushrooms turn soft and juicy. It is best with roti, lacha paratha or naan, and some raita. A good pick for vegetarians who like mushrooms and want something with texture.

dishes.name: Dal Fry
dishes.short_description: Yellow lentils tempered with garlic, cumin and onion, simple and comforting.
dishes.long_description: Dal Fry is yellow lentils cooked soft and finished with a tempering of cumin, garlic, onion and tomato fried in oil or ghee. The texture is thick but pourable and the taste is savoury and mildly spiced. It is a staple everyday dish and goes best with jeera rice, or with roti or naan. A papad on the side adds crunch, and chaas or lassi suits it well. A simple choice for guests who want light, familiar comfort food.

dishes.name: Dal Tadka
dishes.short_description: Yellow lentils finished with a sizzling tempering of garlic, cumin and red chilli.
dishes.long_description: Dal Tadka is lentils cooked until soft, then topped with a tadka, a sizzling mix of ghee, garlic, cumin and dried red chilli poured over at the end. This gives a fragrant, slightly smoky aroma and a medium level of spice. The dal is smooth and easy to eat. Order it with jeera rice for a classic pairing, or with roti or naan, and add a papad and some chaas. A good everyday comfort dish for any guest.

dishes.name: Dal Makhni
dishes.short_description: Black lentils and kidney beans simmered long with butter and cream until velvety.
dishes.long_description: Dal Makhni is black lentils and kidney beans simmered slowly with tomato, butter and cream until the dal turns thick, dark and velvety. The flavour is rich, buttery and mild with a smoky depth from the long cooking. It is lovely with naan or roti, and also goes well over jeera rice, with a papad on the side. Chaas or lassi suits it. A favourite for vegetarians, families and anyone who likes a creamy, hearty dal.

dishes.name: Chole Masala
dishes.short_description: Chickpeas simmered in a tangy, spiced onion-tomato masala.
dishes.long_description: Chole Masala is chickpeas cooked until soft in a dark, tangy onion-tomato masala with chole spices and ginger. The gravy is thick, savoury and medium in spice, with a lightly sour note. It is classically eaten with kulcha, and roti also works well. A bowl of raita, chaas or lassi balances the spice. A filling, satisfying vegetarian choice for guests who want a hearty dish with plenty of flavour.

dishes.name: Chole Karhai
dishes.short_description: Chickpeas cooked wok-style with capsicum in a peppery tomato masala.
dishes.long_description: Chole Karhai takes chickpeas and cooks them wok-style, with chunky capsicum and onion in a thick tomato-pepper masala. The chickpeas stay tender, and the vegetables add a fresh crunch and a peppery tang. It is medium to hot in spice and not as dark as regular chole. Kulcha and roti are the usual accompaniments, and raita, chaas or lassi help with the heat. A good pick for chickpea fans who want a livelier version.

dishes.name: Babycorn Mushroom Shabnam Masala
dishes.short_description: Baby corn and mushrooms in a rich, shahi-style creamy masala.
dishes.long_description: Shabnam is a rich, shahi-style preparation, and this version brings baby corn and mushrooms into a smooth, creamy masala with cashew and onion. The gravy is mellow and lightly sweet with mild to medium spice, while the baby corn gives a gentle crunch and the mushrooms add softness. Naan, garlic naan or roti go well, as does jeera rice. Raita, chaas or lassi on the side finish it off. Good for vegetarians who like richer gravies.

dishes.name: White Butter Chicken
dishes.short_description: Chicken in a creamy white cashew-cream gravy, mild and buttery.
dishes.long_description: White Butter Chicken is a pale, creamy twist on butter chicken. Tender chicken pieces come in a white gravy of cashew, cream and butter, without the red tomato base, so the taste is mild, smooth and gently sweet. It is thick enough to cling to bread. Eat it with naan, garlic naan or roti, or over jeera rice, with chaas or lassi. A good choice for guests who want a rich, low-heat chicken curry.

dishes.name: Chicken Kheema Masala
dishes.short_description: Minced chicken cooked in a thick, spiced onion-tomato masala.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Kheema Masala is minced chicken cooked down with onion, tomato, ginger, garlic and warm spices into a thick, scoopable masala. The texture is soft and crumbly rather than saucy, and the flavour is savoury with medium heat. It is a good match for naan, garlic naan or roti, and also works with jeera rice. Chaas or lassi on the side cools it. Suited to guests who like hearty, minced-meat dishes that are easy to eat with bread.

dishes.name: Butter Chicken
dishes.short_description: Chicken in a smooth tomato-butter and cream gravy, mild and slightly sweet.
dishes.long_description: Butter Chicken is one of the most loved dishes on the menu: tender chicken in a smooth makhani gravy of tomato, butter and cream. The sauce is mild, rich and slightly sweet. It is made for dipping naan or garlic naan, and roti or jeera rice work well too. Add chaas or lassi to the meal. Great for families, children and anyone who wants a creamy, gentle chicken curry.

dishes.name: Spicy Butter Chicken
dishes.short_description: Butter chicken in a creamy tomato gravy with an extra chilli kick.
dishes.long_description: Spicy Butter Chicken keeps the creamy tomato-butter base of the classic but turns up the chilli, so the sweetness of the gravy meets a noticeable heat. The sauce is smooth and rich, with a red, glossy look. It goes well with naan, garlic naan or roti, and also with jeera rice. Chaas or lassi on the side softens the spice. Choose it if you like butter chicken but want it with more bite.

dishes.name: Chicken Tikka Masala
dishes.short_description: Tandoor-grilled chicken tikka in a thick, creamy, medium-spiced masala.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Tikka Masala is made from chicken marinated and grilled in the tandoor, then simmered in a thick tomato-onion masala with cream. You get smoky, charred pieces of chicken in a savoury, medium-spiced gravy that is richer in spice than butter chicken. Naan, garlic naan or roti are the usual partners, and jeera rice works too. Chaas or lassi balances it. A dependable choice for guests who want a flavourful, familiar chicken curry.

dishes.name: Chicken Handi
dishes.short_description: Chicken slow-cooked in a heavy pot with a rich, medium-spiced masala.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Handi is chicken cooked slowly in a heavy clay-style pot so the masala becomes thick, rich and well blended, with onion, tomato, yogurt and spices. The flavour is deep and medium in spice. It comes in Half, which is enough for about two people, and Full, which feeds three to four, so it works well for sharing. Serve with naan, garlic naan, roti or jeera rice, and chaas or lassi.

dishes.name: Chicken Mughlai Leg Curry
dishes.short_description: Chicken leg pieces in a rich, mildly spiced Mughlai-style gravy.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Mughlai Leg Curry uses chicken leg pieces, cooked on the bone in a rich Mughlai-style gravy of onion, yogurt, nuts and aromatic spices. The meat is juicy and comes off the bone easily, while the sauce is smooth, mild to medium in spice and slightly creamy. Eat it with naan, garlic naan or roti, or spoon it over jeera rice, with chaas or lassi alongside. Good for guests who prefer bone-in chicken and mellow, rich flavours.

dishes.name: Afghani Chicken
dishes.short_description: Chicken in a creamy, mild, white-pepper gravy with a gentle smoky note.
dishes.long_description: Afghani Chicken is chicken in a pale, creamy gravy flavoured with white pepper, cream and a little cashew, giving a mild, aromatic taste with a gentle, savoury depth. There is very little chilli. The sauce is smooth and moderately thick. It pairs well with naan, garlic naan or roti, and jeera rice is a good side. Chaas or lassi suits it. A good option for guests who like rich, mild chicken without red masala.

dishes.name: Chicken Masala
dishes.short_description: Chicken in a classic onion-tomato masala, medium-spiced and savoury.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Masala is a straightforward restaurant-style curry: chicken pieces in a thick onion-tomato gravy with ginger, garlic and ground spices. The flavour is savoury and rounded, medium in spice, without much cream, so it tastes more of the masala itself. It is a good partner for naan, garlic naan or roti, and works with jeera rice. Chaas or lassi on the side. A safe choice for guests who want a classic everyday chicken curry.

dishes.name: Chicken Kolhapuri
dishes.short_description: Chicken in a hot, spicy Maharashtrian-style red chilli and coconut gravy.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Kolhapuri is a hot, spicy Maharashtrian-style chicken curry built on red chilli and coconut. The gravy is deep red and fiery, with a nutty warmth from the coconut that rounds out the heat. It is medium thick and bold. Pair it with naan, garlic naan, roti or plain jeera rice, and keep chaas or lassi at hand. Best for guests who love real spice in their non-veg dishes.

dishes.name: Chicken Karhai
dishes.short_description: Chicken wok-cooked with chunky capsicum in a peppery tomato masala.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Karhai is chicken cooked wok-style in a thick tomato masala with black pepper, ginger and chunky capsicum and onion. The gravy is tangy and peppery and the vegetables keep some bite. It is medium-hot and less creamy than most curries on the menu. Naan, garlic naan, roti and jeera rice all go well, and chaas or lassi softens the pepper. A good choice for guests who like robust, tangy flavours.

dishes.name: Bhuna Chicken
dishes.short_description: Chicken in a thick, dry-roasted onion-tomato masala with deep flavour.
dishes.long_description: Bhuna Chicken is cooked by frying the masala down until the onion and tomato turn thick, dark and almost dry, so the chicken is coated in concentrated flavour rather than swimming in sauce. The taste is deep, savoury and medium-hot. Tear naan, roti or lacha paratha and wrap pieces of chicken in it, or serve with jeera rice, with chaas or lassi on the side. Suits guests who like thick, strongly flavoured chicken.

dishes.name: Methi Murgh Malai
dishes.short_description: Chicken in a creamy gravy with fenugreek leaves, mild and aromatic.
dishes.long_description: Methi Murgh Malai pairs chicken with fresh fenugreek leaves in a smooth, cream-based gravy. The creaminess is mild and slightly sweet, and the methi adds an aromatic, gently bitter edge that keeps it from feeling heavy. Spice is low. Serve it with naan, garlic naan or roti, or over jeera rice, with chaas or lassi. A good fit for guests who enjoy the flavour of methi and prefer mellow, creamy chicken dishes.

dishes.name: Palak Chicken
dishes.short_description: Chicken cooked in a smooth, mildly spiced spinach gravy.
dishes.long_description: Palak Chicken cooks chicken in a smooth spinach puree with garlic, onion and gentle spices. The gravy is green, fresh-tasting and earthy, with a mild to medium level of spice and a touch of cream. Tear into naan, garlic naan or roti, or pour it over jeera rice, and add chaas or lassi on the side. A good choice for guests who want a lighter-tasting, vegetable-forward chicken curry.

dishes.name: Lahori Chicken
dishes.short_description: Chicken in a robust, ghee-rich Lahori-style masala with ginger and green chilli.
dishes.long_description: Lahori Chicken is a bold, ghee-rich chicken curry in the Lahori style, with plenty of ginger, green chilli, tomato and ground spices. The masala is thick, glossy and full-flavoured, with a clear kick of heat. It is medium to hot. Naan, garlic naan or roti are the right bread for it, and jeera rice also works. Chaas or lassi helps cool things down. Suited to guests who like hearty, spiced, unfussy chicken.

dishes.name: Murgh Mussallam
dishes.short_description: Whole-chicken style dish in a rich, creamy Mughlai gravy, made for sharing.
dishes.long_description: Murgh Mussallam is a whole-chicken style dish: chicken cooked in a rich, thick Mughlai gravy with onion, yogurt, cashew and cream, with a mild to medium spice and a deep, aromatic flavour. It comes in Half, enough for about two people, and Full, which serves three to four, so it suits a group. Eat it with naan, garlic naan or roti, or jeera rice, and chaas or lassi on the side.

dishes.name: White Chicken
dishes.short_description: Chicken in a pale, creamy cashew gravy that is mild and smooth.
dishes.long_description: White Chicken is chicken in a pale, silky gravy made from cashew, cream and onion, flavoured lightly with white pepper and cardamom. There is no red chilli, so the taste is mild, mellow and slightly sweet. The gravy is smooth and moderately thick. It is best with naan, garlic naan or roti, or with jeera rice, plus chaas or lassi. Suitable for children and for anyone who prefers gentle, creamy food.

dishes.name: White Mutton
dishes.short_description: Tender mutton in a pale, creamy cashew gravy, mild and rich.
dishes.long_description: White Mutton is mutton cooked slowly until tender and served in a pale gravy of cashew, cream and onion, lightly aromatic with white pepper and cardamom. The taste is rich, mild and a little sweet, and the sauce is smooth and thick. It goes well with naan, roti or lacha paratha, or jeera rice, with chaas or lassi on the side. A good choice for mutton lovers who prefer a mellow, creamy curry to a spicy one.

dishes.name: Mutton Rogan Josh
dishes.short_description: Mutton in a deep red, aromatic gravy of onion, yogurt and spices.
dishes.long_description: Mutton Rogan Josh is a well-loved mutton curry: tender mutton in a deep red, aromatic gravy built on onion, yogurt and warm spices. The sauce is thick and glossy with a rounded, savoury flavour and medium heat, without being creamy. It is best with naan, roti or lacha paratha, and jeera rice also suits it. Chaas or lassi balances the spice. A natural pick for mutton lovers who want a classic, full-flavoured red curry.

dishes.name: Karhai Mutton
dishes.short_description: Mutton cooked wok-style with capsicum in a peppery tomato masala.
dishes.long_description: Karhai Mutton is mutton cooked wok-style in a thick tomato masala with black pepper, ginger and chunky pieces of capsicum and onion. The flavour is peppery, tangy and robust, with a medium to hot kick, and the gravy is thick rather than creamy. Take it with naan, roti or lacha paratha, or jeera rice, and cool things down with chaas or lassi. Good for guests who enjoy mutton with a bold, tangy character.

dishes.name: Mutton Handi
dishes.short_description: Mutton slow-cooked in a heavy pot in a rich, deeply spiced masala.
dishes.long_description: Mutton Handi is mutton cooked slowly in a heavy clay-style pot with onion, tomato, yogurt and spices, until the meat is tender and the masala thick and rich. The taste is deep, savoury and medium in spice. It comes in Half, enough for about two people, and Full, which serves three to four, so it is a good dish for sharing. Eat with naan, roti, lacha paratha or jeera rice, with chaas or lassi.

dishes.name: Bhuna Mutton
dishes.short_description: Mutton in a thick, dry-roasted onion-tomato masala with concentrated flavour.
dishes.long_description: Bhuna Mutton is mutton cooked until the masala is fried down to a thick, dark, almost dry coating around each piece. The flavour is concentrated, savoury and medium-hot, built on roasted onion, tomato and ground spices. There is little free gravy, so tear naan, roti or lacha paratha and pick up the meat with it. Jeera rice is a good side, and chaas or lassi helps. Suits guests who love strong, deeply browned mutton flavours.

dishes.name: Chicken Angara
dishes.short_description: Chicken in a smoky, fiery red gravy with a strong chilli kick.
dishes.long_description: Chicken Angara is chicken in a smoky, fiery red gravy named after glowing coals. The sauce is thick and deep red, with a charred, roasted aroma and a sharp, upfront heat. It is one of the spicier chicken dishes on the menu. Serve with naan, garlic naan or roti, or jeera rice, and keep a glass of chaas or lassi handy. Meant for guests who enjoy bold, smoky heat in their chicken.

dishes.name: Methi Chicken
dishes.short_description: Chicken with fresh fenugreek leaves in a savoury, aromatic masala.
dishes.long_description: Methi Chicken cooks chicken with fresh fenugreek leaves in an onion-tomato masala, giving a savoury gravy with a distinct green, slightly bitter aroma. It is less creamy than the malai version and sits at medium spice, with garlic and ginger in the background. Eat it with naan, garlic naan or roti, or jeera rice, with chaas or lassi on the side. Good for guests who enjoy the earthy taste of methi.

dishes.name: Dal Gosht
dishes.short_description: Lentils cooked with tender mutton in a thick, spiced, hearty gravy.
dishes.long_description: Dal Gosht is lentils cooked together with mutton, so the dal becomes thick and meaty and the mutton turns very tender. The flavour is savoury and warmly spiced at a medium level, with garlic, ginger and a tadka on top. It is filling and homely. Eat it with naan, roti or lacha paratha, or jeera rice, with chaas or lassi. A good choice for guests who want something hearty that combines dal and mutton in one bowl.

dishes.name: Mutton Masala
dishes.short_description: Mutton in a classic thick onion-tomato masala, savoury and medium-spiced.
dishes.long_description: Mutton Masala is tender mutton pieces in a thick, restaurant-style gravy of browned onion, tomato, ginger, garlic and ground spices. The flavour is savoury and full, medium in heat, and the sauce is hearty without being creamy. It works well with naan, roti or lacha paratha, and with jeera rice. Chaas or lassi balances the spice. A reliable pick for guests who want an everyday mutton curry without any twist.

dishes.name: Methi Mutton Malai
dishes.short_description: Mutton and fenugreek leaves in a mild, creamy gravy.
dishes.long_description: Methi Mutton Malai combines tender mutton with fresh fenugreek leaves in a smooth cream gravy. The cream and cashew keep it mild and slightly sweet, while the methi brings a gentle bitterness and aroma that balances the richness. Spice is low. Serve with naan, roti or lacha paratha, or over jeera rice, with chaas or lassi. A good choice for guests who like mutton in a mellow, creamy sauce rather than a spicy one.

dishes.name: Lahori Mutton
dishes.short_description: Mutton in a robust, ghee-rich Lahori-style masala with ginger and green chilli.
dishes.long_description: Lahori Mutton is mutton cooked in a bold, ghee-rich Lahori-style masala, with plenty of ginger, green chilli, tomato and ground spices. The gravy is thick and glossy, with strong flavour and a clear kick of heat, medium to hot. It is best scooped up with naan, roti or lacha paratha, and jeera rice also works. Chaas or lassi cools it down. For guests who like their mutton robust, spiced and generous with ghee.

dishes.name: Mutton Kheema Gotala
dishes.short_description: Minced mutton scrambled-style with onion, tomato and spices, thick and hearty.
dishes.long_description: Mutton Kheema Gotala is minced mutton cooked in a thick, scrambled-style masala, with the mince, onion and tomato all tossed together into a loose, coarse mixture. The taste is savoury and meaty, with medium-to-hot spice and a toasty depth. It is a good fit for naan, roti or lacha paratha, and some guests like it with jeera rice. Chaas or lassi on the side. Suited to guests who love minced mutton and want it with plenty of texture.

dishes.name: Mutton Kheema Masala
dishes.short_description: Minced mutton in a thick, savoury masala with peas and medium spice.
dishes.long_description: Mutton Kheema Masala is minced mutton simmered with onion, tomato, ginger, garlic and warm spices, usually with green peas, into a thick, moist masala. The texture is soft and crumbly and the flavour is deep, savoury and medium in heat. It is easy to scoop with naan, roti or lacha paratha, and also goes with jeera rice. Add chaas or lassi. A good, filling pick for guests who like mince-based dishes.

dishes.name: Methi Mutton
dishes.short_description: Mutton with fresh fenugreek leaves in a savoury, slightly bitter masala.
dishes.long_description: Methi Mutton cooks mutton with fresh fenugreek leaves in an onion-tomato masala, with a distinctive green aroma and a slightly bitter note that cuts through the richness of the meat. The gravy is thick, savoury and medium in spice, and not creamy. Take it with naan, roti or lacha paratha, or jeera rice, with chaas or lassi on the side. A good choice for mutton lovers who enjoy earthy, herbal flavours.

dishes.name: Mutton Kolhapuri
dishes.short_description: Mutton in a hot, spicy Maharashtrian-style red chilli and coconut gravy.
dishes.long_description: Mutton Kolhapuri is tender mutton in a fiery red gravy of red chilli and coconut, in the hot, spicy Maharashtrian style. The heat is strong and the coconut adds a nutty warmth underneath. The gravy is thick and deeply coloured. Naan, roti or lacha paratha suit it well, as does jeera rice, and chaas or lassi is useful for the spice. For mutton lovers who really like heat.

dishes.name: Prawns Masala
dishes.short_description: Prawns in a thick, savoury onion-tomato masala with medium spice.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Masala is prawns cooked in a thick onion-tomato masala with ginger, garlic and ground spices. The prawns stay firm and juicy, and the gravy is savoury, a little tangy and medium in heat. It is a good match for jeera rice, or roti or naan, with chaas or lassi on the side. A natural choice for seafood lovers who want a classic, no-fuss prawn curry.

dishes.name: Prawns Tawa Masala
dishes.short_description: Prawns tossed on a hot tawa in a thick, spiced masala with a roasted edge.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Tawa Masala is prawns cooked quickly on a hot flat tawa with onion, capsicum and a thick masala that clings to each piece. It is a drier dish than a regular curry, with a roasted, savoury taste and medium to hot spice. Enjoy it with roti or naan, or alongside jeera rice, with chaas or lassi. For seafood lovers who like their prawns coated in masala rather than served in a loose gravy.

dishes.name: Prawns Karhai
dishes.short_description: Prawns cooked wok-style with capsicum in a tangy, peppery tomato masala.
dishes.long_description: Prawns Karhai cooks prawns wok-style in a tomato masala with black pepper, ginger and chunky capsicum and onion. The flavour is tangy, peppery and lively, and the vegetables add a fresh bite against the tender prawns. Spice is medium to hot, and the gravy is thick. Order it with jeera rice, roti or naan, and a glass of chaas or lassi. A good pick for seafood lovers who like bold, tangy flavours.

dishes.name: Brain Masala
dishes.short_description: Goat brain cooked soft in a spiced onion-tomato masala.
dishes.long_description: Brain Masala is goat brain cooked gently with onion, tomato, ginger, garlic and spices into a soft, creamy-textured masala, usually served as a thick, semi-dry dish. The flavour is rich, savoury and peppery with medium spice. It is a traditional favourite for guests who enjoy offal. Eat it with naan, roti or lacha paratha, or jeera rice, with chaas or lassi on the side. Not for everyone, but loved by those who know it.

dishes.name: Ravas Masala
dishes.short_description: Ravas fish, also called Indian salmon, in a spiced onion-tomato masala.
dishes.long_description: Ravas is Indian salmon, and Ravas Masala serves pieces of this fish in a spiced onion-tomato gravy with a coastal feel. The fish is soft and flaky, and the masala is tangy, savoury and medium to hot. Fish pieces may contain small bones. It goes best with jeera rice, or with roti or naan, and chaas or lassi alongside. A good choice for fish lovers who want a spicy, home-style curry.

dishes.name: Paya Masala
dishes.short_description: Goat trotters slow-cooked in a thick, spiced, gelatinous gravy.
dishes.long_description: Paya Masala is goat trotters simmered for a long time until the meat is soft and the gravy turns thick and slightly sticky from the natural gelatin. The flavour is deep, savoury and warmly spiced, with medium heat and plenty of ginger and garlic. It is meant to be eaten with naan, roti or lacha paratha, or with jeera rice, and chaas or lassi alongside. A traditional pick for guests who enjoy rich, slow-cooked, bone-in dishes.

dishes.name: Anda Masala
dishes.short_description: Boiled eggs in a thick, savoury onion-tomato masala with medium spice.
dishes.long_description: Anda Masala is boiled eggs simmered in a thick onion-tomato masala with ginger, garlic and everyday spices. The eggs soak up the gravy, which is savoury, a little tangy and medium in heat. It is simple, filling and comfort food. Eat it with roti, naan or jeera rice, and add chaas or lassi on the side. A good choice for guests who want an easy, familiar egg curry.

dishes.name: Half Fry Anda Masala
dishes.short_description: Half-fried eggs set in a thick, spiced onion-tomato masala.
dishes.long_description: Half Fry Anda Masala uses half-fried eggs, with a set white and a soft yolk, placed in a thick onion-tomato masala. When you break the yolk it runs into the gravy and makes it richer. The masala is savoury and medium in spice. It goes well with roti or naan, or with jeera rice, and chaas or lassi suits it. A good choice for egg lovers who enjoy a soft, runny yolk with their curry.

dishes.name: Anda Curry
dishes.short_description: Boiled eggs in a lighter, thinner home-style onion-tomato curry.
dishes.long_description: Anda Curry is boiled eggs in a thinner, more spoonable gravy than the masala version, built on onion, tomato and mild spices. The sauce is light, slightly tangy and medium to mild in heat, which makes it good for pouring over rice. Eat it with jeera rice, roti or naan, and chaas or lassi alongside. A simple, homely choice for egg lovers who like a bit more gravy.

dishes.name: Exotic Veg in Sauce
dishes.short_description: Stir-fried exotic vegetables in a sauce of your choice, glossy and savoury
dishes.long_description: Exotic Veg in Sauce is a mix of stir-fried vegetables such as broccoli, baby corn and bell peppers coated in a glossy sauce. The vegetables stay crisp-tender. Eat it with fried rice or noodles to soak up the sauce. A colourful pick for vegetarians. Guests choose the sauce: Soy Basil, Kung Pao, Plum Chilli Garlic, Black Bean, Onion Pepper or Sichuan.

dishes.name: Paneer in Sauce
dishes.short_description: Soft paneer cubes tossed in a glossy sauce of your choice
dishes.long_description: Paneer in Sauce has cubes of soft paneer and onion and capsicum coated in a glossy sauce. The paneer is mild and creamy, so it takes on the sauce well. It goes nicely with fried rice or noodles. A popular choice for vegetarians who want something substantial. Guests choose the sauce: Soy Basil, Kung Pao, Plum Chilli Garlic, Black Bean, Onion Pepper or Sichuan.

dishes.name: Mushroom and Bamboo Shoot in Sauce
dishes.short_description: Mushrooms and bamboo shoots in a sauce of your choice, earthy and crunchy
dishes.long_description: Mushroom and Bamboo Shoot in Sauce pairs soft sliced mushrooms with crunchy bamboo shoots in a glossy sauce. The mix gives an earthy flavour and a nice contrast of textures. Best with steamed or fried rice. Suits vegetarians who like mushrooms. Guests choose the sauce: Soy Basil, Kung Pao, Plum Chilli Garlic, Black Bean, Onion Pepper or Sichuan.

dishes.name: Veg Manchurian Gravy
dishes.short_description: Fried vegetable balls in a savoury soy-garlic sauce
dishes.long_description: Veg Manchurian Gravy is made of fried vegetable balls in a soy-garlic sauce. The balls are crisp outside and soft inside, and they soften further as they soak up the sauce. It is thick, savoury and a little tangy. Usually eaten with fried rice or Hakka noodles. A familiar, comforting favourite for vegetarians.

dishes.name: American Chopsuey Veg
dishes.short_description: Crispy fried noodles topped with a sweet-and-sour vegetable sauce, tangy and crunchy
dishes.long_description: American Chopsuey Veg is a heap of crispy fried noodles topped with a sweet-and-sour sauce full of vegetables. The noodles stay crunchy at first, then soften as the sauce soaks in. It is tangy, a little sweet and fun to eat with a spoon and fork. A good choice for vegetarians and kids.

dishes.name: Exotic Thai Curry Veg

dishes.long_description: Exotic Thai Curry Veg is a coconut-based Thai curry with vegetables in a fragrant sauce. The guest picks Red or Green, with the green usually fresher and herbier and the red deeper and spicier. It is creamy and aromatic. Eat it with steamed or fried rice. Suits vegetarians who like a coconut curry.

dishes.name: Chicken in Sauce

dishes.long_description: Chicken in Sauce is stir-fried chicken pieces with onion and capsicum coated in a glossy sauce. The chicken is soft and juicy. dishes.long_description: Prawns in Sauce has prawns stir-fried with onion and capsicum and coated in a glossy sauce. The prawns are firm and juicy. Best with fried rice or noodles. dishes.name: Lamb Pot Rice
dishes.short_description: Pot-style rice with tender lamb in a savoury, mildly spiced sauce
dishes.long_description: Lamb Pot Rice is pot-style rice served with pieces of lamb in a thick, savoury sauce, so the rice stays moist and well coated. The lamb is meaty and carries a deeper, richer flavour than chicken. It is spooned from the pot and eaten as a one-dish meal. Suits guests who enjoy mutton-style meat and want a filling, comforting plate.

dishes.name: Fish Pot Rice
dishes.short_description: Pot-style rice with soft fish pieces in a savoury, lightly spiced sauce
dishes.long_description: Fish Pot Rice is pot-style rice served with fish pieces in a savoury sauce that keeps the rice soft and moist. The fish is delicate and flaky, so it gives a lighter, gentler bite than meat versions. It is eaten straight from the pot as a single-bowl meal. A good choice for fish lovers who want something comforting without too much heat.

dishes.name: Caramel Pudding
dishes.short_description: Chilled custard-style dessert with soft caramel and a smooth texture
dishes.long_description: Caramel Pudding is a custard-style dessert set smooth and soft, topped with sweet caramel. It is served chilled and is gentle and sweet. It is usually eaten with a spoon at the end of the meal. Suits guests who like mild, creamy desserts. Egg is listed as a cautious note.

dishes.name: Gulab Jamun
dishes.short_description: Two soft fried milk dumplings soaked in sugar syrup, served warm
dishes.long_description: Gulab Jamun is a portion of 2 pieces: soft, round milk-based dumplings fried and soaked in sugar syrup. They are tender, sweet and syrupy. Usually eaten warm with a spoon after a rich biryani or gravy meal. Suits guests with a sweet tooth.

dishes.name: Bottled Water
dishes.short_description: Sealed bottled drinking water, served chilled or at room temperature
dishes.long_description: Bottled Water is sealed packaged drinking water. It is plain and refreshing, and a good match for spicy biryani, tandoor and Indo-Chinese dishes when you want to cool your palate without adding any flavour or sweetness to the meal.

dishes.name: Cold Drinks
dishes.short_description: Bottled soft drinks served chilled, in the usual fizzy flavours
dishes.long_description: Cold Drinks are bottled soft drinks served chilled. They are sweet, fizzy and refreshing, and many guests order them with biryani, kebabs and rice dishes. Ask your waiter which brands and flavours are available today.

dishes.name: Chaas
dishes.short_description: Chilled spiced buttermilk, thin, salty, tangy and very refreshing with meals
dishes.long_description: Chaas is spiced buttermilk made from thinned yoghurt with salt, cumin and a few herbs. It is thin, tangy and cooling, and it helps to settle a heavy or spicy meal. Usually drunk chilled alongside biryani or gravies.

dishes.name: Lassi
dishes.short_description: Thick, sweet, chilled yoghurt drink, creamy and cooling
dishes.long_description: Lassi is a sweet yoghurt drink blended thick and served chilled. It is creamy, smooth and cooling. It is often ordered with biryani or spicy gravies to take the heat off. Suits guests who like sweet drinks.

dishes.name: Fresh Lime Water
dishes.short_description: Fresh lime squeezed into chilled water, served sweet or salted
dishes.long_description: Fresh Lime Water is fresh lime juice mixed with chilled still water. You can ask for it sweet or salted. It is light, sharp and refreshing, and not as heavy as a soft drink. A simple, clean drink to go with biryani, kebabs or rice dishes, and a good way to cut through spice.

dishes.name: Fresh Lime Soda
dishes.short_description: Fresh lime with chilled soda, fizzy, sweet or salted
dishes.long_description: Fresh Lime Soda is fresh lime juice topped with chilled soda water, which gives it fizz. You can ask for it sweet or salted. It is sharp, bubbly and refreshing, and a favourite with rich biryani and fried food.

dishes.name: Chatpata Lime Water
dishes.short_description: Tangy-spiced lime water with a zesty masala kick
dishes.long_description: Chatpata Lime Water is the tangy-spiced version of lime water, with lime juice in still water and a pinch of chaat-style masala. It is sour, salty and a little spicy. Best when you want something more flavourful than plain lime water.

dishes.name: Chatpata Lime Soda
dishes.short_description: Tangy-spiced fizzy lime soda with a zesty masala kick
dishes.long_description: Chatpata Lime Soda is the tangy-spiced version of lime soda, with lime juice, soda water and a pinch of chaat-style masala. It is fizzy, sour, salty and a little spicy. A zippy drink to cut through rich food.

dishes.name: Mojito
dishes.short_description: Mocktail of mint, soda and lime in four flavours
dishes.long_description: Mojito is a mocktail of mint, lime and soda, served over ice. Flavours are Mint, Pineapple, Kalakhatta and Strawberry. Mint is the classic, fresh and sharp; Pineapple is fruity and sweet; Kalakhatta is sweet-sour with a tangy edge; Strawberry is sweet and berry-flavoured. Chilled and fizzy.

dishes.name: Ice Tea
dishes.short_description: Chilled iced tea in Lemon or Peach flavour
dishes.long_description: Ice Tea is chilled sweetened tea served over ice, in two flavours: Lemon and Peach. Lemon is tart and refreshing, and Peach is sweeter and fruitier. It is a light drink to have on a warm day.

dishes.name: Watermelon Juice
dishes.short_description: Fresh, naturally sweet watermelon juice served chilled, light and very refreshing
dishes.long_description: Watermelon Juice is fresh watermelon blended into a light juice and served chilled. It is naturally sweet, watery and cooling, with no heavy flavours added. Order it plain and chilled. A refreshing drink to go with spicy or heavy food.

dishes.name: Blue Mist
dishes.short_description: Bright blue fruity cooler in the style of blue curacao
dishes.long_description: Blue Mist is a bright blue cooler in the style of blue curacao, served chilled over ice with soda. It tastes sweet and citrusy with a light fizz. It is a mocktail-style drink and a colourful pick for guests of all ages.
